It keeps a registry (inventory) of agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center, applies access control through Microsoft Entra, and gives admins visibility and security oversight through Defender and Purview.
flashcards.detail: Entra Agent ID gives an agent an identity, while Agent 365 is where admins see and govern the whole fleet. Both address the risk of invisible, unmanaged agents.

flashcards.front: Large language model (LLM)
flashcards.back: A machine learning model trained on very large amounts of text to understand and generate language. It powers Copilot's responses, but it only knows organizational data when that data is supplied as grounding.
flashcards.detail: Microsoft states that prompts and data accessed through Microsoft Graph are not used to train the foundation models. The model reasons over what it is given.

flashcards.front: Grounding (retrieval-augmented generation)
flashcards.back: Giving a language model relevant, current information, such as the user's permitted files, emails, and chats or web results, along with the prompt so its answer is based on facts rather than just its training. It is also called retrieval-augmented generation.
flashcards.detail: Grounding is trimmed to what the user can already access, which is why Copilot does not expose data beyond existing permissions. Oversharing, not the model, is the risk.

flashcards.front: Microsoft 365 Backup: what it protects and how restore works
flashcards.back: Microsoft 365 Backup protects SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts and Exchange Online mailboxes. Each workload has its own backup policy, and the recovery window on a policy can be 3 months, 6 months, 1 year or 2 years. SharePoint sites and OneDrive accounts are restored by rolling back to a prior point in time (to the same or a new URL); mailboxes can be restored in full or at item level to the same or a new folder.
flashcards.detail: It is built for ransomware and mass-deletion recovery at scale, not for long-term compliance retention. Retention policies keep content for legal or regulatory reasons, whereas Backup returns a site, drive or mailbox to a known-good moment.

flashcards.front: Setting up Microsoft 365 Backup (roles and billing)
flashcards.back: Setting up Microsoft 365 Backup requires the SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator role. Billing is pay-as-you-go through an Azure subscription (you need Owner or Contributor on it, plus a resource group and region), and you pay for the data protected, while restores are not charged. After billing is linked, you create backup policies for OneDrive, SharePoint and Exchange in Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup.
flashcards.detail: Customers onboarding after April 1, 2026 use the pay-as-you-go setup under the Billing node of the admin center, which adds budget alerts and lets backup costs be split across several Azure subscriptions (departmental billing).

flashcards.front: Pay-as-you-go billing for Microsoft 365 services
flashcards.back: Some Microsoft 365 services are not licensed per user but metered against an Azure subscription through pay-as-you-go billing in the Billing node of the Microsoft 365 admin center. Non-Copilot examples include Microsoft 365 Backup, extra SharePoint storage and High Volume Email. An admin creates a billing policy that links an Azure subscription, resource group and region to the service.
flashcards.detail: A missing or deleted Azure subscription link is a common reason a metered service stops working. Copilot-related consumption is governed separately through spending policies in Copilot Cost management.

flashcards.front: Custom organization themes in the Microsoft 365 admin center
flashcards.back: In Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Custom themes, an admin defines the default theme that everyone sees in the top navigation bar, plus up to four additional group themes. A group theme can be assigned to up to five Microsoft 365 groups, and each theme has General, Logos and Colors tabs (logo images must be reachable over HTTPS, with an alternate logo for dark mode).
flashcards.detail: The default theme applies to everyone who is not matched by a group theme, and it cannot be renamed or deleted until the other themes are gone. Group themes are how a subsidiary or brand gets its own look inside one tenant.

flashcards.front: Company branding on the Microsoft Entra sign-in page
flashcards.back: The sign-in page and Access Panel pages that users see are branded through Microsoft Entra company branding (logo, background image or color, banner text), which is separate from the Microsoft 365 admin center theme that colors the navigation bar once users are inside the apps. Branding can be set per language and applies to the tenant's sign-in experience.
flashcards.detail: If a question asks where to change what users see before they authenticate, the answer is Entra company branding; if it asks about the in-app header color and logo, it is the organization theme.

flashcards.front: Network connectivity insights in the Microsoft 365 admin center
flashcards.back: Health > Network connectivity shows network assessments and insights collected from the tenant's own clients. Location data comes from one of three sources: Windows Location Services opt-in (off by default, needs at least two Wi-Fi-connected PCs per site with OneDrive for Windows), admin-added locations with LAN subnets, or results of the Microsoft 365 network connectivity test run at an office. Reports Reader can view it; Service Support Administrator configures it.
flashcards.detail: It is not available in GCC Moderate, GCC High or DoD tenants. Because fixes happen at specific offices, the page is organized by location, not just a tenant-wide average.

flashcards.front: Network assessment score (0 to 100)
flashcards.back: A network assessment condenses TCP latency, download speed and UDP connection quality into a score from 0 to 100, compiled daily, excluding Microsoft-owned networks so the result reflects the customer's own network design. A score of 80 is the healthy baseline where regular user complaints should not occur; 60 is acceptable and 40 or below means users might experience issues. History for the past 30 days is shown.
flashcards.detail: The score is evidence for an ISP, WAN or local-breakout conversation: a low score at one office points to that office's perimeter design rather than to a Microsoft 365 service outage (which Service health would show).

flashcards.front: Service health email notifications
flashcards.back: On the Service health page (Health > Service health), an admin selects Customize > Email to receive notifications of new incidents and status changes for their tenant. Up to two email addresses can be set, with a choice of incidents, advisories or both, and the services to follow; a single issue can also be followed through Manage notifications for this issue. The preference is per admin account. Service Support Administrator and Helpdesk Administrator can view Service health.
flashcards.detail: Service health tells you about Microsoft-side incidents and advisories affecting your tenant. Message center, by contrast, announces upcoming changes. Reporting a problem you do not see listed is done with Report an issue.

flashcards.front: Copilot in Teams meetings: organizer options and the transcription policy
flashcards.back: Organizers choose During and after the meeting, Only during the meeting, or Off for Copilot in a meeting. Only during the meeting relies on temporary speech-to-text that is not saved, while During and after the meeting needs a transcript. Off disables Copilot and also turns off recording and transcription. The tenant transcription policy (AllowTranscription in the Teams meeting policy) interacts with the option: with transcription Off and During and after selected, licensed users cannot use Copilot unless another permitted participant starts transcription.
flashcards.detail: Copilot in Teams meetings needs the Copilot add-on license and is not available in end-to-end encrypted meetings. The admin center shortcut under Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions opens the Teams admin center.

flashcards.front: Which license enables which AI service
flashcards.back: Licensing differs by service. Microsoft Copilot is a per-user add-on (included in Microsoft 365 E7) that is assigned to each user, ideally through group-based licensing. Microsoft Agent 365 is licensed per user (included in E7, add-on for E5/A5/Business Premium) and at least one user must hold a qualifying license to enable it. Copilot Studio usage and many agent experiences are billed in Copilot Credits through capacity or pay-as-you-go. Security Copilot is provisioned as Security Compute Units, not per user.
flashcards.detail: Assigning a license requires a usage location on the user. Owning a SKU in the tenant does nothing for a user until the license is assigned directly or by a group.

flashcards.front: SharePoint Advanced Management: site lifecycle controls
flashcards.back: SharePoint Advanced Management (SAM) manages content sprawl with a site ownership policy (minimum owner or admin counts, with notifications), inactive site policies that notify owners, and site attestation requests in which owners confirm a site is still needed and its permissions are right. It also offers catalog management for grouping sites, change history reports covering 180 days and a view of recent site property changes from the last 30 days.
flashcards.detail: These controls reduce stale, ownerless sites that Copilot would otherwise ground on. SAM is included with a Microsoft Copilot license, which is why it appears in Copilot readiness guidance.

flashcards.front: SharePoint Advanced Management: block download and Conditional Access for sites
flashcards.back: SAM lets an admin tie a Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policy to a SharePoint site by using an authentication context, and create a block download policy that prevents moving or downloading files from SharePoint and OneDrive sites and Teams meeting recordings. These sit alongside restricted access control (limit a site to a group) and Restricted Content Discovery (hide a site from search and Copilot).
flashcards.detail: Choosing the right one depends on the verb in the requirement: hide from search and Copilot, restrict who can open, require a compliant device, or stop downloads each map to a different control.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Search in SharePoint and Copilot: bookmarks and acronyms
flashcards.back: Admins curate authoritative answers for Microsoft Search with bookmarks (promote key resources) and acronyms (define internal terminology). The same curated content is used by Microsoft Copilot Search. Microsoft Search in the Microsoft Copilot app is on by default and can be controlled under Settings > Search & intelligence.
flashcards.detail: Bookmarks and acronyms change what is surfaced for a query, not who has permission to the underlying content.

flashcards.front: Mail contacts, mail users and guest users
flashcards.back: A mail contact is an external email address listed in the address book with no sign-in and no mailbox in the tenant. A mail user has a sign-in account in the directory but an external mailbox. A guest user is an external identity invited into the tenant through Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration that can be given access to groups, teams and sites. Contacts are created in the Exchange or Microsoft 365 admin center.
flashcards.detail: Choose a contact when people only need to find and email someone outside, and a guest when the person must open shared resources.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Entra Password Protection: global and custom banned password lists
flashcards.back: Entra Password Protection checks every password change or reset against a global banned password list that Microsoft maintains automatically from Entra telemetry (it cannot be disabled and its contents are not published) and an optional custom banned password list of up to 1,000 organization-specific base terms such as brand, product and location names. Fuzzy matching and substitution handling block variants, so only the base terms need listing.
flashcards.detail: Add the base term, not every variation: 'Contoso' covers 'Contoso!1' and similar. The custom list needs Microsoft Entra ID P1.

flashcards.front: Entra Password Protection for on-premises Active Directory
flashcards.back: Extending Password Protection to AD DS uses a DC agent installed on domain controllers (a password filter DLL plus service) and a Password Protection proxy service on a domain-joined server that forwards policy downloads from Entra ID. Domain controllers never contact the internet, no schema changes or new ports are required, and password hash sync is not needed. The policy applies only where the DC agent runs, so it should be on every domain controller.
flashcards.detail: Partial deployment is supported for testing but is not secure, because a client can change its password through a DC that lacks the agent.

flashcards.front: Authentication methods policy
flashcards.back: The Authentication methods policy (Entra ID > Authentication methods > Policies, managed by at least the Authentication Policy Administrator) is the recommended place to enable methods such as Microsoft Authenticator, FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, Temporary Access Pass and SMS for specific groups. The legacy per-tenant MFA and SSPR method settings could no longer manage authentication methods after September 30, 2025. Authentication strengths can then require specific method combinations in Conditional Access.
flashcards.detail: The policy decides which methods are allowed; authentication strength decides which of those a Conditional Access policy will accept for a given resource.

flashcards.front: SSPR requirements: registration, number of methods and writeback
flashcards.back: For self-service password reset, users must be in scope and have registered the required number of methods (one or two, set by the admin). Administrator accounts always use a strong two-method reset policy regardless of tenant settings. If a user's password is mastered in on-premises AD (synchronized, pass-through or federated), SSPR works only when password writeback is configured; otherwise the user is told to contact the admin.
flashcards.detail: Admin roles are always held to the stronger two-method policy even if the tenant policy only requires one, so test SSPR with a standard user, not an administrator.

flashcards.front: External collaboration settings for guest users
flashcards.back: Microsoft Entra external collaboration settings control who can invite guests (for example members only, admins and the Guest Inviter role, or anyone), what guests can see in the directory (guest user access restrictions, limited by default), and which domains guests may come from via an allow or deny list. These apply to B2B collaboration and are separate from SharePoint external sharing and Teams external access.
flashcards.detail: A guest can be blocked at several layers (Entra, SharePoint, Teams). When an invitation fails or a guest cannot reach a resource, check each layer.

flashcards.front: Cross-tenant access settings
flashcards.back: Cross-tenant access settings define inbound and outbound B2B collaboration and B2B direct connect behavior with specific partner organizations. They let an admin accept the partner's MFA and device compliance claims, so a guest does not have to satisfy MFA twice, and can limit which users, groups and apps are reachable.
flashcards.detail: Default settings apply to every organization; organization-specific settings override them for named partner tenants.

flashcards.front: Bulk user management with Microsoft Graph PowerShell
flashcards.back: Microsoft Graph PowerShell connects with Connect-MgGraph and the scopes needed, such as User.ReadWrite.All, then uses cmdlets like Get-MgUser, New-MgUser and Update-MgUser, usually driven from Import-Csv for bulk work. The Microsoft Entra admin center also offers CSV templates for bulk create, bulk invite and bulk delete operations. The older MSOnline and Azure AD PowerShell modules are retired and should not be used for new scripts.
flashcards.detail: Asking for the least privilege applies to scripts too: request only the Graph permission scopes the task needs and sign in with an account holding a suitable role.

flashcards.front: Defender for Office 365 preset security policies
flashcards.back: Preset security policies apply Microsoft's recommended settings without per-setting tuning: Standard protection, Strict protection and Built-in protection. Built-in protection gives baseline Safe Links and Safe Attachments coverage to users who are not in Standard, Strict or a custom policy. Standard and Strict are off until an admin turns them on and chooses recipients (users, groups or domains). They are found under Email & collaboration > Policies & rules > Threat policies > Preset security policies in the Microsoft Defender portal.
flashcards.detail: Preset policies take precedence over custom threat policies for the users they cover, so adding a user to Strict overrides a custom anti-phishing policy for that user.

flashcards.front: Anti-phishing, anti-spam and anti-malware threat policies
flashcards.back: Threat policies in the Defender portal include anti-phishing (impersonation protection for users and domains, mailbox intelligence and spoof intelligence), anti-spam, anti-malware, Safe Links and Safe Attachments. Exchange Online Protection supplies anti-spam and anti-malware for every mailbox; Defender for Office 365 adds Safe Links, Safe Attachments and advanced anti-phishing.
flashcards.detail: Priority accounts get extra visibility and tagging for executives who are targeted, but the protection itself comes from the policies applied to them.

flashcards.front: Alert policies and alerts in Defender for Office 365
flashcards.back: Alert policies define activities or threats that raise an alert, with a category and severity. Default policies cover common detections, and admins can add custom policies. Alerts appear in the Defender portal and correlate into incidents in Microsoft Defender XDR so one attack is investigated as a single story rather than as separate email, endpoint and identity alerts.
flashcards.detail: Triage starts from the incident, then drills into the alert's evidence such as the message, URL or user, and uses Threat Explorer in Plan 2.

flashcards.front: Automated investigation and response (AIR)
flashcards.back: AIR, part of Defender for Office 365 Plan 2, starts an automated investigation when certain alerts fire, such as a user-reported phish or a malicious URL click. It collects evidence, assesses the threat and proposes remediation (for example soft-deleting messages or blocking senders) for an approver to accept or reject.
flashcards.detail: Plan 1 does not include AIR or Threat Explorer; Plan 1 focuses on prevention and real-time detections.

flashcards.front: Attack simulation training: simulation techniques and training campaigns
flashcards.back: Attack simulation training (Defender for Office 365 Plan 2) lets admins launch simulated phishing using techniques such as credential harvest, malware attachment, link in attachment, link to malware and drive-by URL, and then assign training to users who fall for them. Training campaigns assign training modules without a simulation. Results and repeat-offender data show who needs more training.
flashcards.detail: A simulation only tests behavior; the training assignment is what changes it, so exam scenarios often pair a simulation with an automatic training follow-up.

flashcards.front: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) in Microsoft Purview: current vs classic
flashcards.back: The current Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) experience in Microsoft Purview covers Microsoft 365, Azure, Fabric and integrated third-party platforms and organizes work around data security objectives such as preventing data exposure in Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions and preventing oversharing. The earlier DSPM for AI (classic) and DSPM (classic) experiences remain available but no longer receive new features.
flashcards.detail: When an older exam or article says DSPM for AI, the current product's equivalent is DSPM with AI observability and Copilot-focused objectives.

flashcards.front: DSPM AI observability and data risk assessments
flashcards.back: AI observability in DSPM shows activity from AI apps and agents, such as oversharing, exfiltration and unusual access patterns, across Microsoft and third-party environments. In DSPM for AI (classic), a weekly data risk assessment automatically runs on the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage, and custom assessments can be added, to find overshared content before or during a Copilot rollout.
flashcards.detail: These tools find and quantify risk; enforcement still comes from sensitivity labels, DLP policies and SharePoint Advanced Management actions.

flashcards.front: Reviewing and responding to DLP alerts
flashcards.back: DLP rules can be configured to generate alerts, with severity thresholds and optional email notification to admins. Admins review the alert in the Microsoft Purview portal or the Microsoft Defender portal, where it can join a Defender XDR incident, look at the matched content and policy, and use Activity explorer to see what happened to the item. User overrides and false positives are used to tune the rule.
flashcards.detail: Alert volume is a tuning signal: very high volume with mostly overrides suggests conditions that are too broad, while no alerts may mean the policy is only in simulation mode.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Copilot naming and license tiers
flashcards.back: Microsoft documentation now calls the licensed experience Microsoft Copilot (formerly Microsoft 365 Copilot) and the chat experience Microsoft Copilot Chat; the app URL moved from m365.cloud.microsoft to copilot.cloud.microsoft. Copilot Chat (Basic) is web-grounded chat included with eligible subscriptions; the add-on license brings work-data grounding, priority in-app access and advanced admin controls. Microsoft 365 E7 includes Copilot, and Microsoft Copilot Business exists for small-business plans.
flashcards.detail: The AB-650 skills outline still uses the Microsoft 365 Copilot name, so expect both names. Network allow lists must include the new copilot.cloud.microsoft endpoints.

flashcards.front: Copilot controls (Copilot Control System): the three pillars
flashcards.back: Copilot controls, the framework known as the Copilot Control System, has three pillars: Security and governance (data security, AI security, compliance and privacy), Management controls (licensing and metering, agent lifecycle, customization) and Measurement and reporting (readiness and adoption, productivity impact, business value, delivered mainly through Copilot Analytics). It covers Copilot, Copilot Chat, prebuilt agents and Copilot Studio agents published to Microsoft 365 channels.
flashcards.detail: It is a framework spread across the Microsoft 365 admin center, Power Platform admin center, Copilot Studio and Purview rather than a single console.

flashcards.front: Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center
flashcards.back: Copilot > Settings has four tabs: User access, Data access, Copilot actions and Other settings. The AI Administrator role can view and change Copilot scenarios, Global Reader can view them. Some entries are real settings (pin Copilot Chat, Copilot in admin centers, AI providers) while others are shortcuts to the Teams admin center, Power Platform admin center, Microsoft Purview or a Cloud Policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
flashcards.detail: Knowing whether a scenario is a setting or a shortcut tells you which role you need: Teams meeting transcription, for example, is ultimately a Teams administrator task.

flashcards.front: Copilot self-service purchases
flashcards.back: The self-service purchase setting for Copilot has three choices: Allow (users can try or buy), Allow trials only (free trial, no purchase, no automatic conversion to paid) and Do not allow. It is managed in Copilot > Settings > User access or with the AllowSelfServicePurchase setting of the MSCommerce PowerShell module, and only Global and Billing administrators can see subscriptions bought this way.
flashcards.detail: Allow trials only is the choice for measuring demand without committing the organization to unplanned licenses.

flashcards.front: Copilot Frontier program setting
flashcards.back: The Copilot Frontier setting controls access to experimental and preview Copilot features in web apps, desktop apps and agents. By default no users have access; an admin can choose No access, All groups of users or Specific user groups. Desktop apps additionally require enrollment in the Microsoft 365 Insider program on the Beta Channel. Preview features are covered by preview terms.
flashcards.detail: Frontier is the way to pilot features before general availability, but it is opt-in per group, not a tenant default.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Copilot in admin centers
flashcards.back: This setting lets users who hold an admin role use Copilot inside the Microsoft 365, Exchange, SharePoint and Teams admin centers. It is allowed for all admins by default and can be changed under Copilot > Settings > User access.
flashcards.detail: It governs the admin-facing assistant, not whether end users have Copilot in Word or Outlook.

flashcards.front: Copilot AI disclaimer
flashcards.back: An AI Administrator can turn on a visible disclaimer, 'AI-generated content may be inaccurate', under Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot AI disclaimer. The admin picks a standard or bold font and can link an internal AI policy from the tooltip. It displays in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneNote and the Copilot app, but not in SharePoint, OneDrive, Whiteboard or Forms. Turning it on creates a Copilot AI Disclaimer policy in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
flashcards.detail: It is a user-awareness control for regulatory expectations; it does not change what Copilot can access.

flashcards.front: Copilot image generation and vision controls
flashcards.back: Copilot image generation is a Copilot actions setting: when off, Copilot does not generate new images and in PowerPoint falls back to stock or brand images. Vision in Microsoft Copilot (sharing a screen or camera with Copilot) is on by default and is disabled by turning off Screen and camera sharing; this does not affect voice. Both are in Copilot > Settings > Copilot actions.
flashcards.detail: These are feature toggles for specific capabilities; they are separate from sensitivity labels or DLP, which govern the data.

flashcards.front: Advanced package uploads for Copilot agents
flashcards.back: Advanced package uploads limit who may upload agent or plugin packages that are advanced, meaning a declarative agent with actions or an MCP server. Options are All users, No users or Specific users or groups. Basic packages (declarative agents with instructions only) stay allowed. It applies only to packages uploaded by the organization's own users.
flashcards.detail: Use it to keep action-capable agents under change control while still letting people build simple instruction-based agents.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Copilot Search
flashcards.back: Copilot Search is a universal search experience that appears as a Search module in the Microsoft Copilot app for users with an eligible Copilot license, at no extra cost, and needs no admin setup. It returns results from Microsoft 365 and from external sources through Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors, can show Copilot Answers, and honors the same permissions and security settings as Copilot. Admins curate bookmarks and acronyms, and Restricted Content Discovery keeps selected sites out of results.
flashcards.detail: Users without the Copilot app get the classic Microsoft Search experience, so the licensing and app, not an admin toggle, decide what they see.

flashcards.front: Third-party AI providers (Anthropic models) in Microsoft Copilot
flashcards.back: Anthropic is a Microsoft subprocessor, so its Claude models used through Microsoft Copilot, Researcher, Copilot Studio and Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps are covered by the Microsoft DPA, product terms and enterprise data protection. They are on by default for most commercial tenants but off by default in the EU, EFTA and UK. Admins manage this under Copilot > Settings > Data access > AI providers for other large language models and can scope it to users or groups. Models labeled with Data Retention need a separate opt-in under Anthropic's own terms.
flashcards.detail: Anthropic models are excluded from the EU Data Boundary. Switching Anthropic off changes which models users can choose; it does not decide who may use a service such as Cowork.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Copilot Cowork
flashcards.back: Cowork is an agentic Copilot experience that carries out multi-step work for a user, such as drafting and sending email, scheduling meetings, creating Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, searching the organization and running scheduled prompts, and it shows each step and asks the user to approve actions. For work or school accounts it is generally available. It can use custom skills (up to 50) and plugins, and Edge browser use is controlled by a tenant Cowork Browsing setting.
flashcards.detail: Because it acts on behalf of the user, it inherits that user's permissions, Conditional Access and DLP rather than having its own broader access.

flashcards.front: Who can use Copilot Cowork: spending policies
flashcards.back: Access to Cowork is granted only by a spending policy in Copilot > Cost Management that includes the user and selects Cowork, even if the credit limit is tiny. The Cowork entry under Agents > All agents no longer controls access, the discovery setting only controls visibility, and turning Anthropic models off only changes the model picker. To keep someone out, leave them out of every policy that selects Cowork, rather than lowering their limit.
flashcards.detail: Credit limits are enforced asynchronously, so a user can start a task after hitting the limit; scope is the real gate.

flashcards.front: Copilot Credits and the Cost management dashboard
flashcards.back: Copilot Credits are the common unit for usage-based billing of eligible Copilot services. In Copilot > Cost management an admin creates spending policies with a scope (all users or security groups), the agents and services included, limits and alerts, model profiles and a billing method (fixed licensing, pay-as-you-go, prepaid capacity packs or a Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan). Auto-apply new services is on by default so new services join existing policies unless it is turned off.
flashcards.detail: Review existing policies because auto-apply means a new billable service can inherit access automatically.

flashcards.front: Credit requests and request policies
flashcards.back: End users can request first-time access to a Copilot service or a higher spending limit, and admins act on these in the Credit requests page. A custom request policy redirects requests to another workflow, for example an internal IT portal or ServiceNow, and a service-specific request policy takes precedence over an all-services one. Redirected requests still appear in the audit view as Handled externally.
flashcards.detail: The Overview tab of Cost management refreshes every four hours, so a user who just hit a limit may not show up immediately.

flashcards.front: Microsoft Copilot usage report
flashcards.back: The usage report is at Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot and can be viewed over 7, 28, 90 or 180 days. Enabled Users are licensed users, Active Users tried a user-initiated Copilot feature in one or more apps, and the Active users rate is active divided by enabled. It also shows adoption by app, prompts submitted to Copilot Chat and a split of Copilot Chat (work) versus (web). Data for a day typically arrives within 48 hours.
flashcards.detail: Use it to find licensed-but-inactive users and per-app adoption; it does not measure business impact, which is the Copilot Dashboard's job.

flashcards.front: Copilot Analytics and the Copilot readiness report
flashcards.back: Copilot Analytics combines Copilot usage data, agent usage data and Microsoft Graph data, and can add outside business metrics. Operational reports live in the Microsoft 365 admin center, strategic reports (such as the Adoption and Impact tabs) in the Copilot Dashboard in Viva Insights, and agent analytics in the Copilot Studio Analytics tab. A Copilot readiness report in the admin center helps plan licensing and rollout.
flashcards.detail: Choosing the right surface is the exam skill: usage by app is the admin center report, trend and impact over time is the Copilot Dashboard.

flashcards.front: Secure and governed data foundation blueprint for Copilot
flashcards.back: Microsoft's blueprint for a Copilot deployment has three pillars: Remediate oversharing, Set up guardrails and Meet regulations. It uses Microsoft Purview and SharePoint Advanced Management (included with a Copilot license) to find high-risk sites, apply interim restrictions where needed, fix access problems and keep guardrails enforced.
flashcards.detail: Interim restrictions such as Restricted Content Discovery buy time, but the lasting fix is correcting permissions and labeling.

flashcards.front: Agent registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center
flashcards.back: Agents > All agents > Registry lists every agent available to the tenant, split into Microsoft agents, external partner-built agents, agents published by your org (line-of-business) and agents shared by their creator. Filters include status, publisher type, channel, platform and data source, and toolbar actions include refresh, export, pinning and customizing the view. An admin can also upload a custom agent manifest as a zip file.
flashcards.detail: Publisher type answers who owns the agent, platform answers what built it, and channel answers where it is available to users.

flashcards.front: Ownerless and unmanaged agents
flashcards.back: The registry tracks agents without owners, which appear when the creator of a shared agent is hard-deleted from the tenant, and unmanaged agents, which were created or managed outside Agent 365 and so lack its risk protection and observability. Admins can filter to ownerless agents and block, delete or reassign them. Risk signals from Purview, Entra and Defender are consolidated per agent for tenants with the E7 or Agent 365 license.
flashcards.detail: Ownerless agents are a lifecycle problem: nobody is accountable for access reviews or retirement, so they are high-priority governance cleanup.

flashcards.front: Reviewing agent requests: publish or reject
flashcards.back: Under Agents > All agents > Requests an admin sees agents waiting in states such as Pending review, Pending update and Pending activate. After checking description, owner, data sources, tools and permissions, the admin selects Publish to store (choosing the audience, optional preinstall, a policy template and admin consent for requested permissions) or Reject submission. Until a Pending update is approved, users keep the previous version.
flashcards.detail: Publishing is scoped, so an approved agent does not have to go to everyone; choose users or groups for a controlled rollout.

flashcards.front: Agent lifecycle actions: block, delete, activate, install
flashcards.back: Admin actions on agents include install or uninstall for selected users, activate (limiting who can create instances), block or unblock, delete with a 30-day recovery window (restore or permanently delete), start or stop for Foundry agents, and assign, add or remove owners. Installing requires reviewing the permissions and granting admin consent.
flashcards.detail: Block stops everyone from using the agent but keeps it in the registry; delete removes it after the recovery window.

flashcards.front: Agent management rules (bulk governance)
flashcards.back: Agent management rules in Agents > Settings find agents that match conditions, let the admin review them and then apply an action in bulk. Supported scenarios are installing Microsoft agents for everyone, reassigning ownerless Agent Builder agents to the previous owner's manager (from the Entra hierarchy), blocking ownerless agents with no usage, applying a policy template to existing agents (a one-time action) and rejecting publish requests older than a set number of days.
flashcards.detail: The template action only evaluates agent instances that have an agent identity, not blueprints.

flashcards.front: Agent settings: access, sharing and user access
flashcards.back: Agent settings include Agent and plugin access (allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft, by your organization or by external publishers), Sharing (All users, No users or Specific users may share Agent Builder agents with the whole organization, while targeted sharing with individuals remains possible), User access (which users and groups can use agents and plugins), feedback sharing and tags.
flashcards.detail: Sharing governs who may share broadly; it does not decide whether an agent is installed or approved.

flashcards.front: Roles for agent management
flashcards.back: Global Administrator and AI Administrator can view insights, view the registry and install, modify and approve agents. Global Reader and AI Reader have read-only access. Security Administrator, Security Reader, Reports Reader and User Experience Success Manager can view insights and the registry but not change agents, and User Account Administrator sees only insights. Product-specific admins such as Power Platform Administrator govern only their own product.
flashcards.detail: Choose AI Administrator for a person who must govern agents and Copilot settings but should not hold Global Administrator.

flashcards.front: Agent tools registry: plugins, skills, MCP servers and connectors
flashcards.back: Agents > Tools > Registry lists the tools available to agents: plugins (packages that bundle capabilities), skills (reusable instructions or workflows), MCP servers (standard servers exposing tools and resources) and connectors (prebuilt links to external systems). Admins can block or unblock a tool, review user requests on the Requests tab, and see Power Platform connector usage (preview), with connector policy handled in the Power Platform admin center.
flashcards.detail: Blocking a tool here prevents agents from using it, which is a different control from blocking the agent itself.

flashcards.front: Agent 365 availability and licensing
flashcards.back: Microsoft Agent 365 became generally available for commercial customers on May 1, 2026. It is licensed per user, works best with Microsoft 365 E5 as a prerequisite, is included in Microsoft 365 E7 and requires at least one user holding a qualifying license to enable it. Extending Entra Conditional Access and ID Governance to agents requires Agent 365 with Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3 at minimum.
flashcards.detail: Licensing the Agent 365 control plane does not by itself create agents; it governs and observes them.

flashcards.front: Agent 365 policy templates
flashcards.back: A policy template bundles policies from Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Purview, SharePoint Online and Microsoft Defender so they can be applied consistently when an agent is published or afterwards. Default controls include Purview audit, sensitive data detection through DSPM, a Purview AI compliance assessment, identity protection, network visibility, lifecycle management, SharePoint access insights and AI real-time protection.
flashcards.detail: Templates are the answer when a requirement says consistent protections for every agent without configuring each tool separately.

flashcards.front: Monitoring agent activity in Agent 365
flashcards.back: Administrators observe all Agent 365 agent activity in Microsoft Defender, while the people who use an agent or are its agent manager can see session details in the Agent Activity tab in Teams or the all agents view in Copilot. Activity is grouped into sessions, which are autonomous (event or time triggered) or conversational. A Teams session ends after 30 minutes of inactivity.
flashcards.detail: Regular users see only their own sessions, which protects privacy while keeping a manager accountable.

flashcards.front: Protecting sensitive data with Purview for Agent 365
flashcards.back: When an Agent 365 agent instance is created it is automatically enabled for auditing, sensitive data detection through data classification and the Compliance Manager assessments for AI regulations. Other solutions such as DLP, Insider Risk Management, Communication compliance, eDiscovery and retention work when the agent instance is included in policies in the same way as a user. Sensitivity labels apply, but encryption without a sensitivity label is not supported.
flashcards.detail: Treat an agent instance like a user for policy scoping: it is not covered by a policy that does not include it.

flashcards.front: Evaluating compliance gaps for agents
flashcards.back: The Purview AI compliance assessment in Compliance Manager continuously evaluates agents against AI regulation templates and shows improvement actions that point to compliance gaps. It is one of the default policies in Agent 365 policy templates, and findings feed the DSPM view of AI risk.
flashcards.detail: Compliance Manager scores the controls; closing a gap still means configuring the policy or process it names.

flashcards.front: Entra Agent ID: blueprints, agent identities and agent users
flashcards.back: An agent identity blueprint is the template and authentication foundation that holds credentials and acquires tokens for the agent identities created from it; policies such as Conditional Access applied to a blueprint affect all of its agent identities. Agent identities have no credentials of their own. An agent's user account is an optional user-like identity for agents that need to act as a user. Traditional service principals and regular user accounts are not recommended for AI agents.
flashcards.detail: Blueprint-level policy is how a fleet of agents is governed with one change instead of hundreds.

flashcards.front: Agent owners, sponsors and managers
flashcards.back: Owners are technical administrators of an agent identity or blueprint (users, including guests, and service principals, not groups) and are optional. Sponsors are business representatives accountable for the agent's purpose and lifecycle without technical access, and at least one sponsor is required for each agent identity and blueprint. Managers are users in the reporting hierarchy who can request access packages for their agents. These relationships are separate from Entra RBAC roles such as Agent ID Administrator.
flashcards.detail: Only owners can re-enable a disabled agent identity or restore a soft-deleted one; sponsors can disable and delete.

flashcards.front: Access packages for agents
flashcards.back: Entitlement management access packages make agent access intentional, time-bound and auditable. An access package for agents can include security group memberships, directory roles and OAuth API permissions, but not application roles, SAP roles or SharePoint Online site roles. The assignment policy targets all agents (and, for agents using service principals, all service principals), with approval stages and expiration. An Identity Governance Administrator creates it, and adding API permissions or directory roles requires Global Administrator.
flashcards.detail: Access packages are the governed route to give a fleet of similar agents the same access, instead of granting permissions to each one ad hoc.

flashcards.front: Lifecycle workflows for agent sponsors
flashcards.back: Entra Lifecycle Workflows has tasks for governing sponsors of agent identities: send email to the manager about sponsorship changes, send email to co-sponsors about sponsor changes, and transfer agent identity sponsorships to the manager. They are mover and leaver tasks available only in workflow templates of those categories and are created by at least a Lifecycle Workflows Administrator in ID Governance.
flashcards.detail: The point is continuity: when a sponsor leaves, the agent should not become unaccountable.

flashcards.front: Conditional Access for agents
flashcards.back: Conditional Access for agents evaluates an agent's access when a token is issued. The target depends on the access pattern: on-behalf-of access targets the users or groups, autonomous app-only access targets the agent identity or blueprint, and agent-user access targets the agent's user account. A policy that targets one subject does not apply to another, so separate policies are needed. It requires Agent 365 plus at least Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3.
flashcards.detail: A policy aimed at the agent identity will not catch the same agent when it signs in through its user account.

flashcards.front: Shadow AI discovery (preview)
flashcards.back: The Shadow AI page in the Microsoft 365 admin center, part of the Frontier preview, helps discover and govern unapproved AI agents running on devices. It needs Defender for Endpoint on the devices, a Microsoft 365 E5 license to view agents, Intune enrollment for managed Windows devices and, for usage metadata, Global Secure Access.
flashcards.detail: It targets agents outside IT's visibility, which is why endpoint and network signals, not the registry alone, feed it.

flashcards.front: Defender real-time protection for Copilot Studio agents
flashcards.back: Defender for AI agents integrates with Agent 365 so discovery, posture assessment and threat detection turn on at onboarding. For Copilot Studio agents, real-time protection scans agent tool invocations during runtime, detects suspicious behavior or cross-prompt injection and blocks the action, raising an alert. It is enabled in the Defender portal (Settings > Security for AI) and completed with a Power Platform administrator, and the Microsoft 365 connector is needed for alerts and hunting.
flashcards.detail: Real-time protection can block even if the connector is not connected, but alerts and incidents will not appear in the Defender portal without it.

questions.question: Contoso adds contoso.com to its Microsoft 365 tenant. The DNS zone already contains an MX record pointing to the current third-party mail provider, an SPF record, and an Autodiscover CNAME. The domain still shows as unverified, and mail flow must not be disrupted during verification. What should you do?
options: Add the TXT record value that Microsoft 365 generated for the domain
Change the MX record to point to the Exchange Online mail servers
Update the SPF record to include spf.protection.outlook.com
Point the Autodiscover CNAME at autodiscover.outlook.com
questions.explanation: Ownership is proven only by the unique TXT verification value Microsoft 365 issues for that domain; publishing it has no effect on mail routing, so the current provider keeps working. Changing the MX record would cut mail over to Exchange Online before mailboxes exist there, which is the disruption the scenario rules out. Updating SPF and repointing Autodiscover are post-verification setup steps for sending and client configuration; neither proves ownership, so the domain would remain unverified.

questions.question: Contoso's HR system sets the department attribute on every new Microsoft Entra user. All users in the Sales department must receive a Microsoft 365 E3 license on their first day, and license assignment must require no per-hire action by IT. Which should you configure?
options: A dynamic security group with a department membership rule, with the license assigned to the group
An assigned security group with the license assigned to the group, with HR adding new hires to it
A dynamic distribution group for the Sales department, with the license assigned to the group
A scheduled PowerShell script that assigns the license to any user whose department is Sales
questions.explanation: Group-based licensing on a dynamic security group means membership recalculates from the department attribute HR already populates, so the license follows automatically with no per-hire step. An assigned group still needs someone to add each new hire, which is exactly the manual action to avoid. A dynamic distribution group is an Exchange Online object, not a Microsoft Entra security group, so it cannot carry a license assignment. A scheduled script works but is custom code to maintain and runs on a delay, so it is more effort than the native feature.

questions.question: Finance users receive Microsoft 365 E5 through group-based licensing on the Finance security group. Compliance requires that Finance users not use Viva Engage, while every other department keeps it. You need to meet the requirement with the least administrative effort. What should you do?
options: Disable the Viva Engage service plan on the Finance group's license assignment
Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks Viva Engage for the Finance group
Disable the Viva Engage service plan directly on each Finance user's account
Replace the group's Microsoft 365 E5 assignment with Office 365 E3 plus the missing add-ons
questions.explanation: Service plans can be toggled per license assignment, so turning off Viva Engage on the Finance group's assignment removes it for every current and future member in one change while leaving other departments untouched. A Conditional Access block is an access workaround, not a licensing change, and leaves the users licensed for a service they are forbidden to use. Disabling the plan per user is repeated effort, and because the group assignment still enables the plan, a direct per-user disable does not take effect while the group grants it. Swapping SKUs is unnecessary churn and does not reproduce E5.

questions.question: Contoso buys licenses through a Cloud Solution Provider partner. The partner must manage Exchange Online for the next 90 days. Contoso requires least privilege and does not want partner accounts created in its own directory. What should you do?
options: Approve a granular delegated admin privileges relationship scoped to the Exchange Administrator role with a 90-day duration
Create a guest account for each partner engineer and make it eligible for Exchange Administrator in Privileged Identity Management
Accept a classic delegated admin privileges relationship and ask the partner to remove it after 90 days
Assign the partner a custom Microsoft Entra role that contains only Exchange permissions, scoped to an administrative unit
questions.explanation: GDAP lets Contoso approve exactly the roles requested, for a set duration, and partner engineers use their own partner-tenant identities, so nothing is created in Contoso's directory. Guest accounts with PIM would achieve least privilege but create accounts in Contoso's tenant that must then be managed and removed. Classic DAP grants broad Admin Agent access with no expiration and relies on the partner to clean up. A custom Microsoft Entra role still has to be assigned to an identity inside Contoso's directory, and custom Entra roles cover directory permissions, not Exchange Online administration.

questions.question: Contoso manages Microsoft 365 Apps with Intune. The IT pilot ring must receive new features as soon as Microsoft releases them. All other devices must receive new features once per month on a predictable date, with no additional feature delay. Which update channels should you assign to the pilot ring and to the other devices, respectively?
options: Current Channel and Monthly Enterprise Channel
Beta Channel and Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel
Current Channel and Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel
Monthly Enterprise Channel and Current Channel
questions.explanation: Current Channel delivers features as soon as they are ready, which fits the pilot ring, and Monthly Enterprise Channel bundles that month's features onto one predictable date (the second Tuesday), which fits everyone else. Beta Channel delivers pre-release builds that are not supported for production devices, and Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel adds a feature delay of months, which the scenario rules out. The Monthly Enterprise Channel and Current Channel pairing is reversed: it would give the pilot ring the predictable cadence and the broad population the unpredictable one.

questions.question: Contoso's reception team needs a reception@contoso.com address. Five staff members must send as the address, and every reply must land in one common Inbox rather than in each person's own mailbox. No SharePoint site, calendar, or Planner should be provisioned, and no additional license should be consumed. What should you create?
options: A shared mailbox
A distribution group
A Microsoft 365 group
A mail-enabled security group
questions.explanation: A shared mailbox provides a single Inbox that delegated users open and send from with Send As permissions, needs no license under the size threshold, and provisions nothing else. A distribution group only fans mail out to each member's own mailbox, so there is no common Inbox for replies. A Microsoft 365 group would give a shared mailbox but also provisions a SharePoint site, calendar, and Planner, which the scenario excludes. A mail-enabled security group delivers to members like a distribution group and exists to grant permissions, not to hold mail.

questions.question: Contoso routes all internet traffic, including Microsoft 365, through an on-premises proxy. Users report choppy audio in Teams calls. The network team confirms the proxy is not overloaded. According to Microsoft 365 network connectivity principles, what should you change?
options: Let Optimize category endpoints, including Teams media, bypass the proxy and egress directly to the internet
Configure split tunneling so that only Default category endpoints bypass the proxy and egress directly
Enable QoS DSCP marking for Teams audio and video traffic on the internal corporate network
Change the Teams meeting policy so that media is carried over TCP instead of UDP
questions.explanation: Microsoft's connectivity principles say Optimize endpoints, which carry latency-sensitive Teams media, should bypass proxies and VPNs and take the shortest path to Microsoft's network. Bypassing only the Default category is backwards: Default traffic is the low-priority bucket that can stay on the normal path. QoS marking helps prioritize media on congested internal links but does not remove the latency added by hairpinning through a proxy. Forcing TCP makes real-time media worse, since UDP is preferred for Teams calls.

questions.question: Contoso's tenant has Microsoft 365 E3 licenses and security defaults enabled. The security team creates a Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device for Exchange Online, but the portal will not let them turn the policy on. What should you do first?
options: Disable security defaults in the Microsoft Entra admin center
Purchase Microsoft Entra ID P2 licenses for the tenant
Set the policy to report-only mode instead of on
Exclude the break-glass accounts from the policy
questions.explanation: Security defaults and Conditional Access are mutually exclusive; while security defaults are on, Conditional Access policies cannot be enabled, so turning security defaults off is the prerequisite. Microsoft 365 E3 already includes Microsoft Entra ID P1, which is all Conditional Access needs; P2 adds risk-based policies and PIM but is not what blocks this. Report-only mode is a good evaluation step, but it does not change the mutual exclusivity, and excluding break-glass accounts is a best practice that comes after the policy can be enabled.
questions.whyTested: This checks that you know Conditional Access replaces security defaults rather than layering on top of it, and that you can separate that blocker from unrelated licensing and best-practice steps that sound like reasonable 'first' actions.

questions.question: Contoso's security policy forbids storing any form of user password credential in the cloud and requires that on-premises account disablement and sign-in hours take effect for cloud sign-ins immediately. Contoso does not want to deploy or maintain an AD FS farm. Which hybrid authentication method should you recommend?
options: Pass-through authentication
Password hash synchronization with seamless single sign-on
Federation with Active Directory Federation Services
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync with password hash synchronization
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication validates each sign-in against on-premises Active Directory through lightweight agents, so no hash is stored in the cloud and on-premises account state, sign-in hours, and password policies are enforced at sign-in time. Password hash synchronization, whether delivered by Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync, stores a hash of the password hash in Microsoft Entra ID, which the policy prohibits. Federation would satisfy both requirements but needs the AD FS infrastructure the organization wants to avoid.
questions.whyTested: Exams stack three hybrid authentication methods that all accomplish 'cloud sign-in for on-prem accounts' to see if you can identify the specific differentiators — whether a password hash ever touches the cloud, and whether on-premises policies are enforced in real time — rather than defaulting to the method Microsoft recommends in general.

questions.question: A Conditional Access policy requires MFA to sign in, and then, for sessions from unmanaged devices, restricts the user to browser-only access with downloads blocked. Which part of the policy is the download-blocking restriction?
options: A grant control
A sign-in risk condition
A named location condition
A session control
questions.explanation: Restricting an already-granted session (like blocking downloads via app enforced restrictions) is a session control. Requiring MFA before access is granted at all is the grant control in this scenario, not the download restriction.
questions.whyTested: This question is testing whether you can tell 'is access allowed at all' apart from 'what happens during an already-granted session' — two conceptually distinct Conditional Access mechanisms that are easy to conflate because both get configured inside the same policy.

questions.question: Several Contoso users clicked links in emails that passed filtering at delivery but were weaponized hours later. You need protection that evaluates the URL at the moment a user clicks it, in email and in Office documents, and that can block the click. Which Defender for Office 365 capability should you configure?
options: A Safe Links policy
Zero-hour auto purge for phishing messages
A Safe Attachments policy with Dynamic Delivery
An anti-phishing policy with impersonation protection
questions.explanation: Safe Links rewrites URLs and checks each one against threat intelligence at time of click, in email and in supported Office apps, and can block the click outright. Zero-hour auto purge is the closest alternative, but it retroactively removes delivered messages once they are judged malicious; it does not inspect at the moment of the click and does not cover links inside Office documents. Safe Attachments detonates file attachments, not URLs. Impersonation protection targets lookalike senders and display names, not links that turn malicious after delivery.

questions.question: A Contoso analyst is investigating an attack that began with a phishing email, continued with malware on the recipient's laptop, and ended with anomalous sign-ins from the recipient's account. The analyst wants a single correlated investigation rather than three separate alert queues. Where should the analyst work?
options: The Incidents queue in the Microsoft Defender portal
Threat Explorer in Microsoft Defender for Office 365
The Risky sign-ins report in Microsoft Entra ID Protection
The device timeline in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender XDR correlates alerts from Defender for Office 365, Defender for Endpoint, and identity signals into a single incident, so the Incidents queue shows the whole attack chain in one place. Threat Explorer is excellent for the email stage but stops there. The Risky sign-ins report covers only the identity stage, and the device timeline covers only the endpoint stage; each of the three distractors is one of the separate queues the analyst wants to avoid.

questions.question: Contoso creates a DLP policy that blocks external sharing of content containing credit card numbers across Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive. Before enforcing it, the compliance team wants two weeks of data on how many legitimate business activities would match, without users becoming aware of the policy. What should you do first?
options: Run the policy in simulation mode with policy tips turned off
Run the policy in simulation mode with policy tips turned on
Turn the policy on with the block action set to allow user overrides
Turn the policy on for a pilot group only and review the incident reports
questions.explanation: Simulation mode records matches and generates reports without taking the configured actions, and leaving policy tips off keeps users unaware, which satisfies both constraints. Simulation with policy tips on still does not block, but it shows tips to users, so they would notice the policy. Allowing overrides still enforces the block for everyone until they override, and a pilot in enforce mode affects real users' work; neither is a measurement-only step.

questions.question: A retention policy set on a SharePoint site says content should be deleted after 3 years. A retention label applied to a specific document in that site says the document must be retained for 7 years. What happens to that document at year 4?
options: It is deleted, because the site-level retention policy takes precedence
It is deleted immediately once any conflict is detected
It is retained, because the longer retention period and the explicit retain instruction win
The system errors and an admin must manually resolve the conflict before any action occurs
questions.explanation: When retention rules conflict, the longer retention period wins, and an explicit retain instruction generally wins over a delete instruction, so the 7-year retention label preserves the document past year 3. Retention conflicts resolve automatically toward preservation, not toward an error state or immediate deletion.
questions.whyTested: This stacks two independent retention mechanisms with seemingly contradictory instructions specifically to test whether you know the actual tie-breaking rule — longer period and 'retain' both win — rather than assuming whichever rule is more specific or was applied most recently automatically takes precedence.

questions.question: Contoso has three requirements for its project documents: they must be encrypted and watermarked, they must be deleted automatically five years after creation, and they must be blocked from being shared with guests in Teams. Which three mappings of requirement to Purview capability are correct? (Choose three.)
options: Encryption and watermark: a sensitivity label
Deletion after five years: a retention label
Blocking sharing with guests: a DLP policy
Watermark: a retention label
Deletion after five years: a sensitivity label
questions.explanation: Sensitivity labels apply protection to content (encryption, markings such as watermarks, permissions), retention labels govern lifecycle (retain and then delete on a schedule), and DLP policies detect sensitive content and act on sharing, including blocking a share with guests in Teams and SharePoint. A retention label has no marking or protection settings, and a sensitivity label has no deletion schedule; those two near-misses swap the jobs of the two label types.

questions.question: Contoso Legal receives a litigation notice. They must send hold notices to 12 named employees, track who has acknowledged them, and reduce the review volume by removing near-duplicate messages and threading email conversations. All users hold Microsoft 365 E5. Which should you create?
options: An eDiscovery (Premium) case
An eDiscovery (Standard) case with a hold on the 12 mailboxes
A Content search scoped to the 12 mailboxes with results exported to PST
A Litigation Hold on the 12 mailboxes and a Communication compliance policy
questions.explanation: Custodian management, hold notifications with acknowledgment tracking, and review-set analytics such as near-duplicate detection and threading are eDiscovery (Premium) features. A Standard case can hold and search the mailboxes, but it has no custodian workflow or analytics. Content search can find and export but cannot hold content or notify custodians. Litigation Hold preserves data, and Communication compliance reviews messages for policy violations; neither notifies custodians or reduces review volume.

questions.question: Nine months ago, an attacker accessed a Contoso executive's mailbox. The executive holds a Microsoft 365 E5 license. Legal needs to know exactly which messages the attacker opened during the compromise. Which capability should you use?
options: Audit (Premium) search in the Microsoft Purview portal
Audit (Standard) search in the Microsoft Purview portal
Threat Explorer in Microsoft Defender for Office 365
Message trace in the Exchange admin center
questions.explanation: The MailItemsAccessed event that identifies individual items that were read is now generated for Audit (Standard) as well, so the deciding factor is retention: Audit (Premium), which Microsoft 365 E5 includes, keeps records for one year by default and still covers activity from nine months ago. Audit (Standard) retains records for 180 days by default, so nine-month-old activity has already aged out. Threat Explorer shows email threat detections and clicks over a recent window, not mailbox reads. Message trace follows delivery through the transport pipeline and shows nothing about what was opened after delivery.

questions.question: A financial services firm needs to prevent its investment banking team from being able to chat with or find the research team in Teams and SharePoint, to avoid a conflict of interest, while both teams still use the same tenant normally. Which feature enforces this?
options: Conditional Access policies scoped by group
Information barriers
Sensitivity labels with encryption
Communication compliance policies
questions.explanation: Information barriers are purpose-built to block communication and collaboration between defined segments of users, exactly the conflict-of-interest scenario described. Conditional Access governs sign-in conditions, not who can communicate with whom, and communication compliance reviews content after the fact rather than blocking contact.

questions.question: An admin wants to grant a user the ability to fully manage DLP policies in Microsoft Purview without granting them any Microsoft Entra directory admin role. How should this be done?
options: Assign the user to an appropriate Purview compliance role group
Assign the user the Global Administrator role
Assign the user the User Administrator Microsoft Entra role
Enable the Microsoft Purview portal for the tenant so existing admins automatically receive edit rights
questions.explanation: Purview compliance permissions are managed through role groups, a separate permission layer purpose-built for compliance solutions like DLP, and do not require any Microsoft Entra directory role. Global Administrator or User Administrator would grant far broader access than is needed or requested, and simply enabling the compliance portal doesn't hand out any permissions by itself — role group membership still has to be assigned explicitly.

questions.question: Contoso's CISO wants a single number that tracks the tenant's security posture across identity, devices, apps, and data, with a ranked list of concrete actions (such as enabling MFA for admins) and the points each action would add. Which should you use?
options: Microsoft Secure Score
Compliance Manager compliance score
Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management exposure score
Microsoft Entra ID Protection risk reports
questions.explanation: Microsoft Secure Score is the posture metric that aggregates identity, device, app, and data recommendations into one score with point-valued improvement actions. Compliance score measures progress against regulatory assessments, not security posture. The exposure score is limited to device vulnerabilities and misconfigurations. ID Protection reports show detected risky users and sign-ins; they do not score configuration or recommend improvements across workloads.

questions.question: An organization is preparing for an ISO 27001 audit and wants to track which required controls Microsoft already fulfills as the cloud provider versus which controls the organization itself must implement and attest to. Which tool is designed for this?
options: Microsoft Secure Score
Defender for Cloud Apps
Compliance Manager
Insider Risk Management
questions.explanation: Compliance Manager translates regulatory requirements into improvement actions and explicitly distinguishes Microsoft-managed actions from customer-responsibility actions, matching the shared-responsibility tracking described. Secure Score measures general security posture rather than mapping to specific regulatory frameworks.

questions.question: After Contoso disables security defaults to adopt Conditional Access, legacy authentication protocols remain blocked for all users until an administrator explicitly re-enables them.
questions.explanation: The legacy authentication block is one of the protections security defaults provides; turning security defaults off removes it along with the rest of the baseline. An organization moving to Conditional Access must recreate that protection as a policy that blocks legacy authentication clients, which is why the switch should be planned with report-only testing rather than assumed to carry over.

questions.question: Contoso uses pass-through authentication as its sign-in method. Enabling password hash synchronization alongside it allows Microsoft Entra ID Protection to detect leaked credentials for Contoso users.
questions.explanation: Leaked-credential detection compares synchronized password hashes against credential dumps, so it requires password hash synchronization even when PTA handles the actual sign-in. Running PHS in parallel also provides a fallback if the PTA agents become unavailable. The misconception is that choosing PTA rules PHS out, or that ID Protection can evaluate credentials it never receives.

questions.question: When a user deletes a OneDrive file that carries a standard seven-year retention label, the file disappears from the user's view but a copy is kept in the Preservation Hold library until the retention period ends.
questions.explanation: A standard (non-record) retention label does not block deletion; it guarantees the content survives it. The deleted file moves to the site's Preservation Hold library, where it stays searchable by eDiscovery until the period expires. Only record and regulatory-record labels actually prevent the user from deleting the item, which is the distinction this statement tests.

questions.question: Communication compliance automatically blocks a flagged message from being sent, similar to a DLP policy in block mode.
questions.explanation: Communication compliance is a detect-and-review workflow that routes flagged communications to reviewers after the fact; it does not block a message from sending the way a DLP policy configured to block can.

questions.question: Insider Risk Management reveals a flagged user's full identity to every reviewer immediately when a case is created.
questions.explanation: Insider Risk Management pseudonymizes user identities in case alerts by default, until an investigator explicitly needs to reveal them, to balance risk detection against employee privacy during review.

questions.question: In a tenant where some users hold Audit (Premium) and others hold only Audit (Standard), audit records generated by an Audit (Standard) user are kept for 180 days by default, regardless of the other users' licenses.
questions.explanation: Audit retention is applied per user based on that user's own license: Premium-licensed users' records default to one year, while Standard-licensed users' records default to 180 days unless an audit log retention policy extends them. One investigator holding Premium does not lengthen retention for the people being investigated.

questions.question: An information barriers policy that blocks the Investment Banking and Research segments from communicating also blocks email between members of the two segments in Exchange Online.
questions.explanation: Information barriers enforce restrictions in Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive: chats, calls, meetings, file sharing, and people search between segments. They do not apply to Exchange Online email; blocking email between groups requires a mail flow (transport) rule. The misconception is assuming one segmentation policy covers every workload.

questions.question: Contoso purchased 100 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, which remain unassigned in the subscription. Managers with Microsoft 365 E3 report that Copilot is unavailable in Word and Outlook, although Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat works for them. What should you do?
options: Assign the Microsoft 365 Copilot license to the managers, for example through a security group
Turn on Copilot for Word and Outlook on the Copilot settings page in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Upgrade the managers from Microsoft 365 E3 to Microsoft 365 E5
Enable web content grounding for the tenant so Copilot can start responding in the apps
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot is an add-on that must be assigned to each user on top of an eligible base license; licenses sitting unassigned in the subscription do nothing, and the free Copilot Chat working is exactly the symptom of an eligible user without the add-on. The admin center Copilot settings page controls behavior for licensed users, not entitlement. Microsoft 365 E5 does not include Copilot either, and web grounding only affects whether responses can use public web content.

questions.question: A licensed Contoso user asks Copilot what the team decided about Project Falcon. Copilot synthesizes an answer from a Teams chat, two emails, and a document, none of which contains that exact phrase, and cites only items the user already has access to. Which component makes this possible?
options: The Semantic Index for Copilot
A Microsoft Graph connector
Microsoft Search keyword indexing alone
The Copilot Studio orchestrator
questions.explanation: The Semantic Index builds an encrypted, Graph-based map of content and relationships across a user's mail, chats, and files, so Copilot can reason about meaning rather than matching keywords, while staying permission-trimmed to what the user can already open. A Graph connector brings external, non-Microsoft 365 content into that index; it is not what grounds native content. Keyword indexing alone would miss items that lack the phrase, and the Copilot Studio orchestrator drives custom agents, not Microsoft 365 Copilot's grounding.

questions.question: A file has been shared tenant-wide with an "Anyone in the organization" link for years, and almost no one who has that access actually needs it. A user with that broad access asks Copilot to summarize the file and Copilot does so. What is the most accurate explanation of what happened?
options: Copilot silently granted the user new access to the file that they did not previously have
This isn't possible — Copilot refuses to summarize any file that has ever had a tenant-wide sharing link
Copilot surfaced content the user already had permission to see, exposing an oversharing risk that already existed
Copilot bypassed SharePoint's permission model entirely because it authenticates using its own separate identity
questions.explanation: Copilot only surfaces content the requesting user already has permission to view, so this behavior reflects pre-existing oversharing rather than any new access Copilot created. It is exactly why oversharing review matters before a broad Copilot rollout.

questions.question: While a full SharePoint permissions review is underway, an admin wants a fast way to keep a set of legacy sites out of both organization-wide search and Copilot summarization, without changing any user's existing site permissions yet. What should they use?
options: Restricted Content Discovery in SharePoint Advanced Management
Restricted access control in SharePoint Advanced Management
A sensitivity label with the Groups & sites scope that sets the sites to private
A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location
questions.explanation: Restricted Content Discovery keeps the selected sites out of organization-wide search and Copilot responses while leaving every permission untouched, which is the only option that satisfies the 'no permission changes yet' constraint (it is the successor to Restricted SharePoint Search, whose new enablement is blocked from July 31, 2026). Restricted access control and a private-site label both change who can access the sites, which is the disruptive step the team is deferring. A Copilot DLP policy acts on sensitive content in Copilot interactions; it does not hide whole sites from search.

questions.question: Contoso already runs DLP and sensitivity labeling. The CISO asks for a view of which generative AI sites and apps employees paste sensitive data into, including non-Microsoft AI sites, along with recommended Purview policies to reduce that risk, with minimal setup. Which should you use?
options: Data Security Posture Management for AI in Microsoft Purview
Cloud app discovery in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Insider Risk Management browsing indicators
Activity explorer in Microsoft Purview
questions.explanation: DSPM for AI is built for this: it reports on sensitive information in prompts to Copilot and third-party AI sites and offers one-click recommended policies such as DLP for pasting into AI sites. Cloud app discovery shows which AI apps are in use and their risk scores, but not what sensitive data was entered or which Purview policies to deploy. Insider Risk Management scores individual users' behavior rather than giving a tenant-wide data view. Activity explorer shows activity on labeled and classified content, not a dedicated AI usage posture.

questions.question: Contoso's 'Highly Confidential' sensitivity label applies markings but no encryption, and Legal does not want to change how the labeled files open. Users who can open those files must not be able to have Microsoft 365 Copilot summarize or quote their content. The files are spread across many sites. What should you configure?
options: A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location and a condition on the sensitivity label
Encryption on the sensitivity label that grants users View but not Extract rights
Restricted SharePoint Search covering the sites that hold labeled files
A retention label with a short deletion schedule applied to the labeled files
