questions.explanation: A DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can stop Copilot from processing content that carries the label, leaving file access and the label itself unchanged. Removing the Extract right through label encryption also keeps Copilot from using the content, but it changes the label to encrypt files, which Legal ruled out. Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) works at the site level, would hide unlabeled content too, and has no effect on files recently opened by or shared directly with the user. A retention label governs deletion, not Copilot behavior.

questions.question: A department wants a lightweight agent that answers questions using only the content of one specific SharePoint site, inheriting that site's existing permissions, built with minimal effort. What is the fastest supported way to create this?
options: Create an agent directly from the SharePoint site
Build a declarative agent in Copilot Studio and add the site as a knowledge source
Deploy a Microsoft Graph connector for the site before building an agent
Build a custom engine agent that calls the SharePoint REST API
questions.explanation: Creating an agent from the SharePoint site itself takes a few clicks, grounds the agent in that site's content, and inherits the site's permissions automatically, which is the fastest supported path. A declarative agent in Copilot Studio with the site as a knowledge source also works and respects permissions, but it is more setup than the scenario needs. SharePoint content is already indexed in Microsoft Graph, so a Graph connector adds nothing, and a custom engine agent is the most effort of all.

questions.question: Contoso's security team wants the Copilot Studio agents built by business units to be visible in Microsoft Entra as first-class identities, so they can be inventoried, included in access reviews, and governed with the same lifecycle tools used for service principals. Which capability provides this?
options: Microsoft Entra Agent ID
A manually created app registration and service principal for each agent
Microsoft Entra workload identity federation
Microsoft Entra Permissions Management
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Agent ID gives agents their own identity objects in Microsoft Entra so they appear in the directory and can be governed like other identities. Creating an app registration per agent is the manual near-miss: it is laborious and depends on each business unit remembering to do it. Workload identity federation lets external workloads such as pipelines obtain tokens without secrets, and Permissions Management is a multicloud entitlement (CIEM) tool; neither represents agents in the directory.

questions.question: Contoso's six SOC analysts want a generative AI assistant inside the Microsoft Defender portal to summarize incidents and write KQL hunting queries. Procurement will not buy per-user AI licenses for the whole company. What should you purchase?
options: Security Compute Units for Microsoft Security Copilot
Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licenses for the six analysts
Copilot Studio message capacity packs
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps licenses for the analysts
questions.explanation: Microsoft Security Copilot is the security-specific assistant embedded in Defender, Entra, Purview, and Intune, and it is purchased as provisioned Security Compute Units rather than per user, so six analysts can share capacity. Microsoft 365 Copilot is the productivity assistant for Office apps and does not provide the Defender experience. Copilot Studio capacity funds custom agents, and Defender for Cloud Apps is a CASB with no AI assistant of its own.

questions.question: An organization wants Copilot to be able to ground answers in content from a third-party wiki that lives outside Microsoft 365, while still respecting that wiki's own access control list. What should be configured?
options: A Microsoft Graph connector for the wiki, with its permissions mapped to the wiki's access control list
A Copilot Studio agent that uses the wiki as a knowledge source through a connector
A nightly export of the wiki into a SharePoint site readable by everyone in the organization
Restricted SharePoint Search with the wiki added to the allowed list
questions.explanation: A Graph connector indexes the wiki into Microsoft Graph and the Semantic Index so Microsoft 365 Copilot can ground on it, and mapping the connector's ACL to the source is what keeps results permission-trimmed. A Copilot Studio agent with the wiki as a knowledge source would let that one agent answer wiki questions, but it does not make the content available to Microsoft 365 Copilot generally. A nightly export readable by everyone discards the wiki's access control list, creating oversharing. Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) only governs SharePoint sites and cannot include an external system.

questions.question: Compliance wants to be able to search, export, and place a legal hold on the actual prompts and responses a specific user exchanged with Microsoft 365 Copilot last quarter. Is this possible, and if so, through what?
options: No, Copilot interactions are ephemeral by design and are never written to any searchable log
Yes, Copilot prompts and responses are captured as audit events, searchable and exportable through Microsoft Purview eDiscovery
Yes, but only by exporting chat transcripts manually from within the Copilot app itself
No, only Copilot Studio agent conversations are logged; Microsoft 365 Copilot chats are not recorded anywhere
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses are captured as audit log events and are searchable, exportable, and placeable on legal hold through Purview eDiscovery, the same as other Microsoft 365 content. This makes Copilot interactions genuinely discoverable, not ephemeral or unlogged.

questions.question: A marketing employee built a Copilot Studio agent that calls an unapproved file-storage connector and published it to Microsoft Teams, where other users can now find it. You must stop users from running the agent now and prevent any future agent from combining that connector with Microsoft 365 data, without affecting other agents. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)
options: Block the agent in the Agents area of the Copilot Control System in the Microsoft 365 admin center so users can no longer run it
Create a Power Platform DLP policy that places the connector in the Blocked group for the environment
Delete the Power Platform environment that hosts the agent so the agent can no longer be invoked
Turn off the Allow web search in Copilot policy in the Cloud Policy service
questions.explanation: Blocking the agent in the Agents area of the Copilot Control System (which grew out of Integrated apps) removes it from users immediately, and a Power Platform DLP policy that classifies the connector as Blocked prevents any agent or flow in that environment from using it going forward. Deleting the environment would also remove every other agent and flow in it, violating the 'without affecting other agents' constraint. The Allow web search in Copilot policy controls whether Microsoft 365 Copilot can use public web results and has nothing to do with connectors.

questions.question: To assign the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on through group-based licensing, the add-on must be assigned by the same group that assigns the user's base Microsoft 365 license.
questions.explanation: Group-based licensing evaluates each assignment independently; the add-on can be assigned by a dedicated pilot group while the base license comes from another group or from a direct assignment. The only requirement is that the user ends up with an eligible base license plus the add-on. Tying the two to one group is a common assumption that would force restructuring licensing groups unnecessarily.

questions.question: Because Microsoft 365 Copilot honors existing permissions, a file shared with 'Everyone except external users' can be surfaced by Copilot to an internal user who has never opened it.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone except external users' grants every internal user permission, so Copilot can legitimately surface the file to any of them whether or not they ever opened it. Honoring permissions is exactly why broad grants like this are the oversharing risk to fix before a rollout; the misconception is treating 'never accessed' as if it meant 'not permitted'.

questions.question: With Restricted SharePoint Search enabled, a user can still have Microsoft 365 Copilot reference a file from a site that is not on the allowed list if that file was shared directly with the user or the user recently opened it.
questions.explanation: Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) limits organization-wide search and Copilot grounding to the allowed sites, but it deliberately keeps content a user owns, has recently accessed, or has had shared directly with them discoverable, since the user already works with it. It is a visibility stopgap for broadly shared sites, not a per-file access control.

questions.question: A SOC analyst can use the Microsoft Security Copilot experience embedded in the Microsoft Defender portal without holding a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license, as long as the tenant has provisioned Security Compute Units and the analyst holds a Security Copilot role.
questions.explanation: Security Copilot is a separate product funded by provisioned Security Compute Units and gated by its own role assignments; per-user Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses play no part. The two products are easy to conflate because both carry the Copilot name, but their licensing models are independent.

questions.question: Contoso assigns Current Channel to an IT pilot ring, Monthly Enterprise Channel to most users, and Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel to a validation lab. Which two statements about this design are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Monthly Enterprise Channel devices receive that month's new features on a single predictable release date
Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel devices receive new features months after Current Channel devices do
Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel devices receive security updates only twice a year
Current Channel devices receive new features on a fixed monthly release date
questions.explanation: Monthly Enterprise Channel bundles the month's features onto one release date, and Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel holds features back so they arrive months after Current Channel users already have them. Every channel, including Semi-Annual Enterprise, still receives security updates monthly; only feature updates are held back. Current Channel ships features as soon as they are ready, which is why its cadence is less predictable than Monthly Enterprise Channel's.

questions.question: Contoso's Cloud Solution Provider partner sends a granular delegated admin privileges (GDAP) relationship request. Which two statements describe what Contoso is agreeing to if it approves it? (Choose two.)
options: The partner receives only the Microsoft Entra roles listed in the request, for the duration specified
Partner staff gain access through their own partner-tenant identities rather than accounts created in Contoso's directory
The relationship automatically includes Global Administrator so the partner can recover the tenant
Contoso cannot end the relationship before its expiration date, because termination is controlled by the partner
questions.explanation: A GDAP relationship is explicitly scoped to the roles named in the request and runs for a defined duration, and partner engineers are mapped to those roles through security groups in the partner's own tenant, so no accounts are created in Contoso's directory. Global Administrator is included only if the partner requests it and Contoso approves it; nothing is added automatically. Contoso can terminate a GDAP relationship at any time from the Microsoft 365 admin center, which is part of what distinguishes it from classic DAP.

questions.question: Contoso's Conditional Access policy for SharePoint Online on unmanaged devices must require MFA, limit users to browser-only access with downloads blocked, and force re-authentication every four hours. Which two of these requirements are implemented as session controls? (Choose two.)
options: Browser-only access with downloads blocked, using app enforced restrictions
Re-authentication every four hours, using sign-in frequency
Requiring MFA before access is allowed
Requiring a compliant device before access is allowed
questions.explanation: App enforced restrictions and sign-in frequency both shape an already-granted session, so they are configured under the policy's Session controls. Requiring MFA is a grant control, since it decides whether access is permitted at all. Requiring a compliant device is also a grant control, and it is not even part of this scenario's requirements; it is included as a near-miss for candidates who associate 'device' with session behavior.

questions.question: Contoso applies a retention policy to all SharePoint sites that retains content for three years and then deletes it. HR applies a retention label that retains for seven years to certain files on the HR site. In year two, an HR user deletes one of those labeled files. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: A copy of the deleted file is preserved in the Preservation Hold library until the seven-year period ends
The site policy's three-year deletion does not remove the labeled file, because the longer retention period wins
The user is prevented from deleting the labeled file while the retention period is in effect
The labeled file is permanently deleted at year three, because the site policy was applied first
questions.explanation: A standard retention label lets the user delete the file from view, but retention preserves a copy in the Preservation Hold library for the remainder of the seven years. When a policy and a label conflict, the longer retention period and the explicit retain instruction win, so the three-year deletion does not apply to labeled files. Deletion is only blocked when an item is declared a record, and which rule was applied first plays no part in the precedence.

questions.question: Eight months ago an attacker compromised a Contoso mailbox. Investigators now need the list of individual messages the attacker read. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: If the mailbox owner was licensed only for Audit (Standard), records from eight months ago have already aged out of the 180-day default retention
If the mailbox owner was licensed for Audit (Premium), the default one-year retention still covers the activity
Assigning an Audit (Premium) license to the user now restores the audit records that already expired
A historical message trace can substitute for the audit records, because it shows which messages were opened
questions.explanation: Audit (Standard) retains records for 180 days by default, so eight-month-old activity is gone, whereas Audit (Premium) retains records for a year by default. The mailbox-access event this investigation depends on (MailItemsAccessed) is now generated for Audit (Standard) too, so retention is what separates the two. Licensing cannot retroactively recreate records that have expired or were never generated. Message trace reports delivery through the transport pipeline over a limited window; it never records which items a signed-in user opened.

questions.question: Contoso configures an Insider Risk Management policy for data theft by departing users and connects the Microsoft 365 HR connector. Which two statements about the resulting alerts are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Alerts display pseudonymized user names until a user with the appropriate role reveals the identity
Resignation and termination dates imported through the HR connector act as triggering events for the policy
The policy blocks the flagged downloads in real time once an alert reaches high severity
Alerts for the policy are generated only after the user's termination date has passed
questions.explanation: Insider Risk Management pseudonymizes identities in alerts by default, and the HR connector supplies the departure dates that trigger scoring for the departing-user policy template. The policy itself detects and scores activity for investigation; it does not block downloads, which would be DLP's job (or adaptive protection feeding a DLP policy). The policy watches a window of activity before and after the departure date, since the risky behavior usually happens before the last day.

questions.question: During a Copilot pilot, a Contoso user shows that Copilot summarized a salary spreadsheet. Investigation finds the file sits on an HR site that was shared with 'Everyone except external users', and the user had never opened it. Which two conclusions are correct? (Choose two.)
options: The user already had permission to the file through the broad sharing grant; Copilot did not create new access
Remediation belongs in SharePoint: remove the broad grant and review the HR site's sharing settings
Copilot cached the spreadsheet from another user's session and served it across accounts
Disabling the Semantic Index for the HR site would have prevented the exposure
questions.explanation: Copilot only surfaces what the requesting user can open, so the spreadsheet was reachable because of the 'Everyone except external users' grant, and the fix is to correct that sharing, which SharePoint Advanced Management's data access governance reports help find at scale. Copilot has no cross-user cache; each response is grounded for the requesting identity. The Semantic Index cannot be disabled per site; hiding a site from Copilot during review is done with Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery).

questions.question: Contoso enables Data Security Posture Management for AI in Microsoft Purview. Which two outcomes can Contoso expect? (Choose two.)
options: Reports showing sensitive information types detected in prompts and responses across Copilot and third-party AI sites
One-click recommended policies, such as a DLP policy that limits pasting sensitive data into AI websites
Automatic blocking of any Copilot response that contains sensitive information
A licensing prerequisite that must be satisfied before Copilot licenses can be assigned
questions.explanation: DSPM for AI provides visibility reports on sensitive data in AI interactions and surfaces recommended policies it can create for you, which is how it bridges discovery to action. It does not itself enforce anything; blocking requires a DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location or endpoint DLP for AI sites. It is also not a licensing gate; Copilot licenses can be assigned whether or not DSPM for AI has ever been opened.

questions.question: An organization is migrating from Tenant A to Tenant B during a merger and wants to reuse its custom domain contoso.com in Tenant B. What must happen before contoso.com can be verified in Tenant B?
options: Nothing; the same custom domain can be verified in both tenants at the same time
Remove the domain from Tenant A's verified domains, then add and verify it in Tenant B
Tenant B must be granted a GDAP relationship to Tenant A before the domain can be verified
A new TXT record must be published for Tenant A only, and Tenant B inherits verification automatically
questions.explanation: A custom domain can only be verified in one Microsoft 365 tenant at a time, so it must be removed from the source tenant's verified domains before the destination tenant can add and verify it. Attempting to verify it in both tenants at once is not supported, which is why domain cutover is typically the last, carefully timed step of a tenant-to-tenant migration.

questions.question: Contoso's service desk must be able to reset passwords for non-administrator users and open support requests with Microsoft. Service desk staff must not be able to reset passwords for users who hold admin roles or modify user accounts. You need to follow the principle of least privilege. Which role should you assign?
options: Helpdesk Administrator
Password Administrator
User Administrator
Service Support Administrator
questions.explanation: Helpdesk Administrator can reset passwords for non-admins (and other helpdesk admins), and it can also create and manage Microsoft support requests, which covers both duties with no account-editing rights. Password Administrator can reset non-admin passwords but cannot open support requests. User Administrator adds the ability to create and modify users and groups, which exceeds least privilege. Service Support Administrator can open support requests and view service health but cannot reset anyone's password.

questions.question: An admin wants a sensitivity label that, when applied to a Microsoft 365 Team, automatically makes the team private and blocks access from unmanaged devices, rather than encrypting any individual file. Which sensitivity label scope must be enabled for this label?
options: Files & emails scope only
Groups & sites scope
Schematized data assets scope
Meetings and calendar events scope
questions.explanation: The Groups & sites scope applies container-level settings — privacy, external access, and unmanaged device restrictions — to the Microsoft 365 Group or Team itself. The Files & emails scope only protects individual documents and messages (meetings are part of that same items scope, not a separate one), and the Schematized data assets scope covers database columns and similar assets in the Purview Data Map; none of those touch a team's container-level settings.

questions.question: Two DLP policies both match the same document, but their configured actions conflict. What determines which policy's action actually takes effect on that document?
options: The policy with the numerically larger priority number is evaluated first and applies its action
The policy with higher priority (a lower priority number, evaluated first) applies its matching rule's action
Both actions are applied simultaneously regardless of the conflict
Whichever policy was created most recently overrides any older, conflicting policy
questions.explanation: DLP policies are evaluated in priority order, where a lower priority number is evaluated first and effectively wins when policies conflict; rules within a policy are then evaluated top-down. Creation date and a numerically higher priority number do not determine precedence — the priority ranking does.

questions.question: Contoso enforces risk-based Conditional Access policies. A user's sign-in is flagged with high sign-in risk because of impossible travel, and the same account separately shows high user risk from a leaked-credential detection. The user completes MFA successfully for the risky sign-in. What is the account's state afterward?
options: The sign-in risk is remediated, but the user risk remains until a secure password change
Both the sign-in risk and the user risk are remediated by the successful MFA
Neither risk is remediated until an administrator dismisses the user risk
The user risk is remediated, but the sign-in risk remains until an administrator confirms it safe
questions.explanation: Sign-in risk is a per-session signal, so satisfying MFA remediates that sign-in. User risk from leaked credentials indicates the password itself is compromised, and it is remediated by a secure password change (self-service through a user-risk policy, or an admin reset); MFA alone does not clear it. Admin dismissal is a manual option, not a requirement, and the claim that user risk clears while sign-in risk lingers reverses which risk each remediation addresses.
questions.whyTested: This checks that you distinguish per-session sign-in risk from account-level user risk, and that you know MFA clears the former while only a password change clears the latter — the two are evaluated and remediated differently, not interchangeably.

questions.question: A retention policy needs to automatically apply to every user in the Finance department, and stay current as employees move into or out of Finance, without an admin manually updating a list of names. Which Microsoft Purview scoping feature should be used?
options: A static scope listing named users
An adaptive scope based on a department attribute query
A sensitivity label auto-labeling policy
A retention label published to the Finance users
questions.explanation: Adaptive scopes dynamically include users, groups, or sites based on attribute queries like department, so the policy's coverage recalculates automatically as attributes or membership change. A static scope would require manual updates every time someone joins or leaves Finance, defeating the requirement. Sensitivity auto-labeling applies protection, not retention, and publishing a retention label only makes it available for users to apply by hand; it does not scope or apply a policy automatically.

questions.question: A Contoso compliance analyst must search the unified audit log for a quarterly review and must not be able to change audit retention policies or any other Purview configuration. The analyst currently holds no roles. You need to follow least privilege. What should you do?
options: Add the analyst to the Audit Reader role group in Microsoft Purview
Add the analyst to the Audit Manager role group in Microsoft Purview
Add the analyst to the Compliance Administrator role group in Microsoft Purview
Assign the analyst the Reports Reader Microsoft Entra role
questions.explanation: Audit Reader grants exactly the View-Only Audit Logs permission needed to search the unified audit log. Audit Manager is the near-miss: it also allows creating and managing audit log retention policies, which the scenario forbids. Compliance Administrator spans most Purview solutions and is far broader than needed. Reports Reader is a Microsoft Entra role for usage reports and does not include audit log search.

questions.question: An admin wants to measure Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption across the organization — which apps it's used in and overall active-user trends — without being able to see the specific content of any individual user's prompts. Which capability should they use?
options: A Microsoft Purview eDiscovery search across each named user's mailbox
Microsoft 365 Copilot usage reports and the Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard
Insider Risk Management case details for each licensed user
Restricted SharePoint Search reporting in the SharePoint admin center
questions.explanation: Copilot usage reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center and the Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard show aggregated adoption metrics like active users and app usage trends without exposing individual prompt content. Seeing a specific user's actual prompts would require an eDiscovery search instead, which is a different, more invasive capability.

questions.question: A company has not purchased any Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licenses, yet an employee reports using "Copilot" to ask general web-grounded questions from within a Microsoft 365 app. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The employee is using Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, included at no extra cost with a Microsoft Entra work account
The company must already have purchased Copilot add-on licenses previously without anyone realizing it
This isn't possible without a paid Copilot add-on license assigned to that specific user
The employee is actually using Microsoft Security Copilot, which is free for every licensed user
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is included with any Microsoft Entra work account at no extra licensing cost and provides web-grounded chat, distinct from the licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on that grounds answers in the organization's own Semantic Index. Security Copilot is a separate, SCU-billed product, not a free option for general use.

questions.question: A custom Copilot Studio agent built by one department is consuming far more usage than its prepaid Copilot Credit capacity (formerly measured in messages) allows. What happens once that prepaid capacity is exhausted, assuming no additional capacity has been purchased?
options: The agent is deleted automatically the moment its prepaid Copilot Credit capacity runs out
Further usage is billed pay-as-you-go if enabled; otherwise the agent may stop responding until the next period
The agent's prepaid capacity silently resets and usage continues with no billing impact
Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses for the entire tenant are automatically suspended until capacity is purchased
questions.explanation: Once prepaid Copilot Credit capacity (formerly messages) is exhausted, further Copilot Studio agent usage draws on metered pay-as-you-go billing if enabled, or the agent may stop responding until the next capacity period if it is not. Monitoring capacity consumption matters because usage does not simply reset immediately, and unrelated tenant-wide Copilot licenses are not suspended.

questions.question: The Message center in the Microsoft 365 admin center reports the real-time operational status of a service outage, while Service health announces upcoming feature changes.
questions.explanation: This has the two reversed: Service health reports real-time operational status and incidents, while Message center announces upcoming planned changes, new features, and deprecations admins need to plan for.

questions.question: In Privileged Identity Management, a user with an active Global Administrator assignment that expires in one month holds the role continuously for that month without activating it, unlike a user with an eligible assignment.
questions.explanation: A time-bound active assignment is standing access for its whole window: the role is always on with no activation, justification, approval, or per-use audit entry. An eligible assignment grants nothing until the user activates it, typically with MFA, a justification, and optionally an approver, for a limited activation duration. Both have an end date, but only eligibility delivers just-in-time access.

questions.question: The EU Data Boundary is a Copilot-specific setting that only affects where Copilot prompts are processed, with no effect on other Microsoft 365 workloads.
questions.explanation: The EU Data Boundary is a tenant-wide data-residency commitment covering the storage and processing of Microsoft 365 data broadly, including but not limited to Copilot prompts, grounding data, and generated responses. It is not a narrow, Copilot-only toggle.

questions.question: Contoso synchronizes its single Active Directory forest with Microsoft Entra Connect. It acquires Fabrikam, whose forest has no network connectivity or trust with Contoso's forest, and must bring Fabrikam users into the same tenant. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync agents can be installed in Fabrikam's forest and run alongside the existing Microsoft Entra Connect server
Cloud Sync does not require network line of sight from Contoso's Microsoft Entra Connect server to Fabrikam's domain controllers
A second active Microsoft Entra Connect server can be installed in Fabrikam's forest and pointed at the same tenant
A forest trust between Contoso and Fabrikam must be created before either tool can synchronize Fabrikam's users
questions.explanation: Cloud Sync's lightweight agents install inside the forest they synchronize and are managed from the Microsoft Entra admin center, so they can cover Fabrikam's disconnected forest while Microsoft Entra Connect keeps handling Contoso's forest; the two tools are supported side by side for different forests. Only one active Microsoft Entra Connect server is supported per tenant (additional servers must be in staging mode), so a second active server is not an option. Neither tool requires a forest trust; Microsoft Entra Connect would need network connectivity to Fabrikam's domain controllers, which is exactly what is missing.

questions.question: Contoso adds the ISO 27001 and GDPR assessments to Compliance Manager, then enables MFA for all administrators. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: The MFA improvement action can contribute points to both assessments at the same time
Actions Microsoft is responsible for appear in each assessment with Microsoft's own test status, without Contoso implementing them
Marking the MFA action as implemented causes Compliance Manager to configure the Conditional Access policy
A 100 percent compliance score means Contoso has achieved ISO 27001 certification
questions.explanation: Improvement actions are shared across assessments, so one control such as admin MFA earns credit wherever a template requires it, and Microsoft-managed actions are tracked with Microsoft's attestation under the shared responsibility model. Compliance Manager tracks and scores; it never configures tenant settings itself. The compliance score is an internal progress measure, not an auditor's certification.

questions.question: A Contoso employee publishes a Copilot Studio agent to Microsoft 365 Copilot, but colleagues cannot find it in their agent list. Which two statements are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: If the tenant requires admin approval for agents, the agent remains unavailable until an admin approves it in the Agents area of the Copilot Control System
An admin can make the approved agent available to specific users or groups rather than to everyone
Publishing from Copilot Studio automatically makes the agent available to every user in the tenant
An admin must first create an app registration for the agent in Microsoft Entra before it can appear
questions.explanation: Shared agents flow through the Agents area of the Copilot Control System (which grew out of Integrated apps), where tenants that require approval hold them until an admin acts, and the admin can then deploy the agent to all users, specific groups, or no one. Publishing alone does not grant tenant-wide availability, which is exactly why the colleagues cannot see it. Copilot Studio handles the agent's identity and registration as part of publishing; the admin does not hand-create an app registration.

questions.question: Contoso needs a group that project managers can email to reach all project leads, and that site owners can use to grant permissions on several SharePoint sites. The group must not provision its own mailbox, SharePoint site, or Planner. Which type of group should you create?
options: A mail-enabled security group
A Microsoft 365 group
A distribution group
A security group
questions.explanation: A mail-enabled security group is both a mail recipient and a security principal, so it can receive email and be used in SharePoint permission grants without provisioning any connected resources. A Microsoft 365 group would also satisfy email and permissions, but it automatically creates a group mailbox, SharePoint site, and Planner, which the scenario excludes. A distribution group receives email but is not a security principal, so it cannot be used to grant SharePoint permissions. A plain security group can be used for permissions but is not mail-enabled.

questions.question: Contoso's legal team asks you to place the shared mailbox contracts@contoso.com on Litigation Hold. The mailbox is accessed only through delegates who hold Microsoft 365 E3 licenses, and no one signs in to it directly. An administrator states that shared mailboxes never require a license. What should you do?
options: Assign an Exchange Online license to the shared mailbox before applying the hold
Apply the hold without a license, since no one signs in to the mailbox directly
Convert the shared mailbox to a user mailbox so the hold can be applied
Apply the hold to each delegate's mailbox instead, since their licenses cover the shared mailbox
questions.explanation: A shared mailbox is license-free only while it stays under the size threshold with no archive, no hold, and no direct sign-in. Placing it on Litigation Hold is one of the conditions that requires an Exchange Online license on the shared mailbox itself. The 'no direct sign-in' rule covers normal delegated use, not holds. Converting to a user mailbox is unnecessary and still needs a license. Delegates' licenses never extend to the shared mailbox object, and holding their mailboxes would not preserve the shared mailbox's content.

questions.question: Contoso requires MFA through Conditional Access. Most users registered SMS as their only method. You need to move users to Microsoft Authenticator with number matching and stop new SMS registrations, without immediately locking out users who have only SMS today. What should you do first?
options: Configure a registration campaign for Microsoft Authenticator in the Authentication methods policy
Apply the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength in the Conditional Access policy
Disable the SMS method in the Authentication methods policy
Enable per-user MFA enforcement for all users in the legacy MFA portal
questions.explanation: A registration campaign prompts users who still rely on weaker methods to set up Microsoft Authenticator at sign-in, with a snooze window, so adoption rises before SMS is switched off; that is the right first move. Requiring phishing-resistant strength would immediately reject SMS sign-ins and also reject Authenticator push, which is not phishing-resistant. Disabling SMS now locks out everyone who has nothing else registered. Per-user MFA is the legacy mechanism Microsoft steers customers away from, and it does not drive Authenticator registration.

questions.question: Contoso wants any document saved to SharePoint that contains credit card numbers to be encrypted automatically, with no action by the user who saved it. Users should keep working on the files normally. Which should you configure?
options: A sensitivity label auto-labeling policy for SharePoint with a label that applies encryption
A DLP policy for SharePoint with an action that encrypts matching content
A mandatory labeling policy that sets a default encrypted label for all documents
An auto-apply retention label policy that targets the credit card sensitive information type
questions.explanation: Service-side auto-labeling scans content in SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange and applies a sensitivity label, including one that encrypts, with no user involvement. The DLP encrypt action is the near-miss: it exists, but it applies only to Exchange email, so it cannot encrypt SharePoint files. A mandatory default label depends on users saving from a client that applies it and would encrypt every document, not just those containing card numbers. A retention label governs how long content is kept and cannot encrypt anything.

questions.question: An organization wants to detect when an employee who is about to resign downloads an unusually large volume of files shortly before their last day, correlated with their HR-flagged departure status. Separately, they want to review whether employees are sharing offensive language in Teams chats company-wide. Which two Purview solutions address these, respectively?
options: Insider Risk Management for the departure scenario, and Communication compliance for the language review
Communication compliance for the departure scenario, and Insider Risk Management for the language review
eDiscovery (Premium) handles both, since its analytics can also flag risky behavior and offensive language
DSPM for AI handles both, since it monitors unusual data access patterns and risky messages
questions.explanation: Insider Risk Management correlates HR signals like departure status with activity like unusual downloads to flag potential data exfiltration. Communication compliance reviews message content for policy violations like offensive language. Swapping the two assigns each tool the job it does not do, eDiscovery is a search/hold tool rather than a behavioral risk detector, and DSPM for AI is scoped to AI interaction risk, not general file-download or chat-content review.

questions.question: A tenant currently relies on Security Defaults for baseline protection. The security team wants a more advanced rule — block sign-in from a specific country except for two named traveling executives — while keeping simple baseline MFA enforced everywhere else with no ongoing manual policy upkeep for every new user. What should they do?
options: Turn off Security Defaults and rebuild its baseline protections, plus the country-based block, as Conditional Access policies
Keep Security Defaults enabled and add a separate Conditional Access policy for the country-based block exception
Leave Security Defaults enabled, since it already supports per-country, per-user exceptions natively
Keep Security Defaults enabled and add the two executives to an exclusion list within Security Defaults
questions.explanation: Security Defaults and custom Conditional Access policies can't run side by side — enabling the granular, per-country exception this scenario needs requires turning off Security Defaults and rebuilding its baseline protections (like tenant-wide MFA) as explicit Conditional Access policies. Security Defaults itself is an all-or-nothing baseline with no per-country logic and no exclusion list of any kind, so neither 'keep it and add an exception' option is possible.

questions.question: Contoso has 1,000 employees with Microsoft 365 E3. All employees need web-grounded AI chat with enterprise data protection. Only the 100 managers need Copilot in Word, Excel, and Teams meetings grounded in organizational data. You need to minimize licensing cost. What should you do?
options: Buy 100 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses for the managers and rely on Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat for everyone else
Buy 1,000 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses so every employee has a consistent Copilot experience
Buy 100 Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses and 900 Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat licenses
Upgrade all 1,000 employees to Microsoft 365 E5, which includes Copilot in the apps
questions.explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat comes with every Microsoft Entra work account at no additional cost and provides web-grounded chat with enterprise data protection, so only the managers need the paid add-on that embeds Copilot in the apps and grounds it in organizational data. Licensing all 1,000 overspends by 900 licenses. There is no separate Copilot Chat license to buy, and Microsoft 365 E5 does not include Microsoft 365 Copilot.

questions.question: Contoso's support team wants Microsoft 365 Copilot to answer questions such as 'what is the status of ticket 4821' using live data from a third-party ticketing system, and to create new tickets on request. What should you build?
options: A Copilot Studio agent with an action that calls the ticketing system's API
A Microsoft Graph connector that indexes the ticketing system's records
A Power Platform DLP policy that allows the ticketing system connector
A SharePoint list synchronized nightly from the ticketing system and an agent grounded on it
questions.explanation: Live lookups and write-backs such as creating a ticket require an action (plugin) that calls the system's API at runtime, which is what a Copilot Studio agent with a connector action provides. A Graph connector is the near-miss: it indexes a copy of the records for search and grounding, so answers can be stale and it cannot create tickets. A Power Platform DLP policy only permits or blocks connectors; it builds nothing. A nightly SharePoint sync is neither live nor capable of taking actions.

questions.question: DSPM for AI reports show many interactions where Copilot surfaced files with an "Anyone in the organization" link that contain sensitive financial terms. The security team wants to move from just seeing this in reports to actually blocking Copilot from including that sensitive content in future responses. What's the necessary next step, and why doesn't DSPM for AI alone accomplish it?
options: Create or tune a Purview DLP policy scoped to Microsoft 365 Copilot, because DSPM for AI reports on risk but does not enforce
Nothing further is needed, because DSPM for AI reports begin enforcing once a risk threshold is reached
Enable Insider Risk Management instead, because it is what actually blocks Copilot responses
Apply a sensitivity label to DSPM for AI itself, which extends its reporting into an enforcement policy
questions.explanation: DSPM for AI is a discovery and reporting capability — it surfaces oversharing and sensitive-data risk in AI interactions, but a separate DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location is what actually enforces: a sensitivity-label condition keeps labeled content out of Copilot processing, and a sensitive-information-type condition blocks prompts that contain that data. Its reports don't self-escalate into enforcement, Insider Risk Management addresses user behavior risk rather than content-level blocking, and a sensitivity label can't be applied to DSPM for AI itself — it's a reporting tool, not a document.

questions.question: Contoso publishes SPF and DKIM records for contoso.com. Attackers still send spoofed messages that appear to come from contoso.com, and some partner mail systems deliver them. Contoso wants receiving systems to reject messages that fail authentication and wants to receive aggregate reports about those failures. What should you publish?
options: A DMARC TXT record with a reject policy and a reporting address
An SPF record that ends with a hard fail (-all) qualifier
A second DKIM selector with a longer signing key
An MX record that routes inbound mail through Exchange Online Protection
questions.explanation: DMARC is the policy layer on top of SPF and DKIM: it tells receiving servers what to do on failure (monitor, quarantine, or reject) and where to send aggregate reports, which covers both requirements. A hard-fail SPF qualifier only signals a failed sender check; it provides no reporting and receivers treat it inconsistently. Another DKIM selector strengthens signing but does not instruct receivers about disposition. Changing the MX record affects how Contoso receives its own mail, not how other organizations handle mail spoofing contoso.com.

questions.question: A new hire's account is created by an HR provisioning script that leaves the usage location attribute blank. An admin then tries to license them through an existing group-based licensing assignment. What happens?
options: The license assigns normally, since usage location only matters for Copilot add-on licenses
The assignment is skipped and flagged as a licensing error until a usage location is set
The system automatically copies the assigning admin's own usage location onto the account
Group-based licensing cannot be used at all unless usage location was set at tenant creation
questions.explanation: Usage location is required before any license can legally be assigned to a profile, and a group member missing it is skipped with a flagged error rather than silently licensed. Usage location matters for every license, not just Copilot, there is no automatic copying from the admin's own account, and group-based licensing works fine elsewhere in the tenant once the attribute is set for that one user.

questions.question: An external auditor needs broad read-only visibility into nearly every Microsoft 365 admin center configuration setting, while a separate analyst only needs to view usage reports and nothing else. Which built-in roles fit the auditor and the analyst, respectively?
options: Global Reader for the auditor; Reports Reader for the analyst
Reports Reader for the auditor; Global Reader for the analyst
Global Administrator for the auditor; Helpdesk Administrator for the analyst
User Administrator for both the auditor and the analyst
questions.explanation: Global Reader mirrors Global Administrator's broad visibility but with no edit rights, suiting the auditor, while Reports Reader is scoped narrowly to usage reports, suiting the analyst. The reversed pairing is wrong, and Global Administrator or User Administrator would grant edit rights far beyond what either person needs.

questions.question: A global company wants its European employees' primary mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint data to physically reside in an EU datacenter while North American employees' data stays in a North American datacenter, all inside one single Microsoft 365 tenant and directory. Which capability enables this?
options: The EU Data Boundary
Multi-Geo
Customer Lockbox
Restricted SharePoint Search
questions.explanation: Multi-Geo lets a single tenant place a given user's own data in a chosen satellite region while remaining one tenant and directory, matching this exact scenario. The EU Data Boundary instead governs whether an entire in-scope tenant's data stays within the EU/EFTA region, not per-user placement across multiple regions within one tenant.

questions.question: A dynamic security group with the rule department -eq "Finance" is used for group-based licensing. When an administrator manually adds a contractor to that group, the contractor receives the group's license.
questions.explanation: Membership of a dynamic group is calculated entirely from its rule; members cannot be added or removed manually, so the attempt is not possible and no license results. To license the contractor, set the attribute the rule evaluates, add the contractor to a separate assigned group that also carries the license, or assign the license directly. The misconception is treating a dynamic group like an assigned group with a helpful default rule.

questions.question: Contoso must prevent frontline workers from recording Teams meetings and must allow only executives to delete chat messages they have sent. Both settings must apply only to the relevant groups and must not change behavior for anyone else. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)
options: Create a meeting policy with cloud recording turned off and assign it to the frontline workers group
Create a messaging policy that allows deleting sent messages and assign it to the executives group
Turn off cloud recording in the Global (Org-wide default) meeting policy
Create a Conditional Access policy that blocks the Teams recording feature for frontline workers
questions.explanation: Teams meeting policies control in-meeting capabilities such as recording, and messaging policies control chat behavior such as deleting sent messages; both can be assigned to a group so that only its members are affected. Changing the Global (Org-wide default) policy alters behavior for every user who has no custom policy, which violates the 'no one else' constraint. Conditional Access governs the conditions of sign-in and session, not individual Teams features such as recording.

questions.question: A university wants students to self-request access to a bundled set of resources — a Team, a SharePoint site, and a licensed app — through a catalog, with a manager approval step and automatic expiration at the end of the semester, instead of an admin manually granting each resource. Which Microsoft Entra ID Governance feature fits?
options: Access reviews
Entitlement management (access packages)
Privileged Identity Management
Conditional Access
questions.explanation: Entitlement management bundles resources into an access package that users can request through a self-service catalog, with approval workflows and automatic expiration built in, exactly matching this scenario. Access reviews recertify access that already exists rather than provisioning it, PIM governs role eligibility, and Conditional Access governs sign-in conditions, not resource bundling.

questions.question: A user tries to install a third-party app that requests permission to read every mailbox in the tenant through Microsoft Graph. The organization wants this kind of high-privilege request to always be reviewed and approved by an administrator rather than left to the individual user. What should be configured?
options: A Conditional Access policy blocking that specific app
An app consent policy requiring admin consent for that permission level
Disabling Microsoft Graph access for the entire tenant
An information barrier between the user and the app
questions.explanation: App consent policies control whether a user can grant consent themselves or whether a request must route to an admin through the admin consent workflow, which directly matches the requirement. Blocking one app with Conditional Access doesn't govern consent for every similar app going forward, disabling Graph tenant-wide would break legitimate integrations, and information barriers govern user-to-user communication, not app permission consent.

questions.question: A broker-dealer must guarantee regulators that a 7-year retention policy on trade communications cannot be shortened or disabled by anyone, including its own Global Administrators, once it is finalized. Which Microsoft Purview feature provides this guarantee?
options: Preservation Lock on the retention policy
A litigation hold placed on each mailbox individually
Customer Lockbox
Information barriers
questions.explanation: Preservation Lock prevents anyone, including a Global Administrator, from turning off or shortening a locked retention policy until its locked duration expires, matching this exact regulatory requirement. A per-mailbox litigation hold doesn't lock the policy itself against admin changes, Customer Lockbox governs Microsoft support engineer access, and information barriers govern communication between user groups.

questions.question: A bank wants to require that administrators sign in using only phishing-resistant authentication methods, such as a FIDO2 security key or certificate-based authentication, rather than accepting any MFA method including SMS. Which Conditional Access control should be configured?
options: A session control that limits sign-in frequency for administrators
A grant control that requires a phishing-resistant authentication strength
A grant control that requires multifactor authentication by any method
Security defaults, which enforce MFA for all administrator roles
questions.explanation: Authentication strength is a grant control that can mandate a specific combination of methods, like phishing-resistant ones, rather than accepting any second factor equally. A plain 'require MFA' control accepts weaker methods like SMS too, a session control only restricts an already-granted session rather than which method was used, and security defaults cannot be customized to this degree.

questions.question: If a security group that is assigned the Exchange Administrator role is onboarded to PIM for Groups, making a user's membership eligible means the user holds Exchange Administrator only while an activated membership is in effect.
questions.explanation: PIM for Groups makes group membership itself just-in-time. Any Microsoft Entra role, app role, or license the group grants is effective only while the user's activated membership lasts, so the role becomes just-in-time without configuring PIM separately on the role. The near-miss is assuming the role assignment to the group bypasses the membership activation.

questions.question: A university creates an access package in entitlement management that bundles a Team, a SharePoint site, and an app role for a semester course. Which two statements about this access package are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: The request policy can be set so that access expires on a fixed date at the end of the semester
The request policy can require the requestor's manager to approve before access is granted
A recurring access review must be configured on the package before it can be published
Students from a partner university cannot request the package, because access packages are internal-only
questions.explanation: Access package policies support lifecycle settings that expire access on a date or after a number of days, and approval stages that can name the requestor's manager as approver. Access reviews on a package are optional, not a publishing prerequisite. External users can be allowed to request packages through connected organizations, which is one of entitlement management's main uses for guest onboarding.

questions.question: A team wants to build a Copilot agent with its own independent reasoning engine and language model, entirely separate from Microsoft 365 Copilot's own orchestrator, trading simplicity for full control over its behavior. Which agent type are they building?
options: A declarative agent
A custom engine agent
An agent created directly from a SharePoint site
A Microsoft Graph connector
questions.explanation: A custom engine agent brings its own independent orchestrator and model, giving full control at the cost of far more development effort. A declarative agent and a SharePoint-grounded agent both build on Copilot's own existing orchestrator and Semantic Index instead, and a Graph connector only indexes content for grounding rather than defining an agent's reasoning engine.

questions.question: An admin wants to stop Copilot in Word from searching the public web for extra context, while leaving its ability to ground answers in the organization's own files and emails untouched. Where should this be configured?
options: The EU Data Boundary configuration for the tenant's Microsoft 365 data
The Allow web search in Copilot policy, configured through the Cloud Policy service
A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location
Restricted SharePoint Search in the SharePoint admin center
questions.explanation: The Allow web search in Copilot policy, configured through the Cloud Policy service (and reached from the Copilot page in the Microsoft 365 admin center), controls whether Copilot can search the public web while leaving grounding in organizational content alone. The EU Data Boundary governs data residency rather than web search, a DLP policy restricts sensitive content in responses rather than toggling web search, and Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) only hides sites that are not on its allowed list from search and Copilot, with no effect on web search.

questions.question: A Contoso user asks Copilot to summarize a supplier's web page. Hidden text on the page instructs Copilot to email the user's recent documents to an external address. Copilot ignores the instruction and only summarizes the visible content. Which protection acted, and what class of attack was attempted?
options: Built-in content safety and prompt shields, defending against cross-prompt injection
A DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location, defending against data exfiltration
Safe Links time-of-click scanning, defending against a malicious URL
Semantic Index permission trimming, defending against oversharing
questions.explanation: Instructions hidden in grounding content that try to hijack the assistant are cross-prompt injection, and Microsoft 365 Copilot's content safety classifiers and prompt shields are the controls designed to detect and ignore them. A Copilot DLP policy filters sensitive content out of responses but does not recognize hidden instructions. Safe Links evaluates URL reputation when a user clicks, not what a page tells an AI to do. Permission trimming limits what Copilot can read, not how it responds to what it reads.

questions.question: A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location prevents cross-prompt injection attacks, because it inspects the grounding content that Copilot reads.
questions.explanation: Copilot DLP policies act on sensitive content: a sensitivity-label condition keeps labeled content out of Copilot processing, and a sensitive-information-type condition blocks prompts that contain that data; they do not look for hidden instructions or stop an injected prompt from steering the model. Cross-prompt injection is addressed by Copilot's built-in content safety and prompt-shielding protections. Conflating the two is treating a data-leak control as a manipulation control.

questions.question: Contoso's HR agent in Copilot Studio must answer open-ended questions from a SharePoint policy library and must walk users through a fixed, scripted sequence when they request paid time off. Which two configurations support this design? (Choose two.)
options: Enable generative orchestration so the agent picks the knowledge source or topic that best fits each message
Author a classic topic with trigger phrases and a scripted dialog for paid-time-off requests
Author a separate classic topic for every possible policy question in the SharePoint library
Switch the agent to classic orchestration only, because generative and classic cannot coexist in one agent
questions.explanation: Generative orchestration lets the model route open-ended policy questions to the SharePoint knowledge source at runtime, while an explicitly authored topic keeps the PTO flow deterministic; the two coexist in the same agent. Authoring a topic per policy question is exactly the manual effort generative orchestration removes, and the claim that the two modes cannot coexist is false, because an agent can combine generative orchestration with authored topics.

questions.question: A Copilot Studio agent needs to call both an approved internal line-of-business connector and a popular consumer social-media connector in the same action. The organization's Power Platform DLP policy places those two connectors in separate classification groups. What happens when the agent tries to combine them?
options: The combination is blocked, because the two connectors fall into different Power Platform DLP classification groups
The combination succeeds, because Power Platform DLP policies apply only to Power Automate flows, not Copilot Studio agents
The combination succeeds, since Copilot Studio agents are automatically exempt from Power Platform DLP enforcement
The combination is blocked only when a separate Purview DLP policy scoped to Copilot interactions is also configured
questions.explanation: Power Platform DLP policies group connectors into classifications and block connectors from different groups from being combined in the same flow or agent action, which is exactly what stops this combination. These policies apply broadly across Power Platform, including Copilot Studio agents, and this block does not depend on a separate Purview DLP policy scoped to Copilot interactions.

questions.question: An admin needs to fully block a specific finance-only SharePoint site from being opened by anyone outside one designated security group, even by users who otherwise hold broad admin permissions. Which capability actually accomplishes this, as opposed to only hiding the site from search and Copilot?
options: Restricted SharePoint Search applied to the finance site
Restricted access control in SharePoint Advanced Management
A sensitivity label scoped to Files & emails applied to the site's documents
Data Security Posture Management for AI reporting
questions.explanation: Restricted access control in SharePoint Advanced Management actually limits who can access a site at all, unlike Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery), which only removes a site from search and Copilot results while leaving every existing permission untouched. A Files & emails-scoped sensitivity label protects individual documents rather than gating access to a whole site, and DSPM for AI only reports on risk rather than enforcing any access restriction.

questions.question: Before a Microsoft 365 Copilot rollout, an admin wants a prioritized list of SharePoint sites that are overshared or contain sensitive content, so remediation effort can focus on the highest-risk sites first. Which capability provides this site-level list?
options: Data access governance reports in SharePoint Advanced Management
Microsoft 365 Copilot usage reports in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Compliance Manager assessment templates in Microsoft Purview
Content explorer in Microsoft Purview, used on its own
questions.explanation: Data access governance reports are built specifically to surface overshared or sensitive SharePoint sites so remediation can be prioritized before a wider Copilot rollout. Usage reports measure Copilot adoption rather than site risk, Compliance Manager tracks regulatory requirements rather than SharePoint sharing risk, and Content explorer shows where labeled content currently sits without prioritizing sites by oversharing.

questions.question: A team uses Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat to draft a project brief, then wants several teammates to keep editing and refining that draft together over the next several days rather than losing it as a one-time chat reply. What should they turn the draft into?
options: A Copilot Page
A Copilot Notebook
A new Teams channel post
A Teams meeting recap
questions.explanation: A Copilot Page turns a chat response into a persistent, shareable canvas that several people can keep open and co-author over the following days. A Copilot Notebook gathers references and chats into a workspace for grounding further prompts; it is not the way to co-edit one drafted document. A channel post and a meeting recap are static outputs rather than live, co-authored drafts.

questions.question: In Contoso's Teams meetings, participants speak English and Spanish. Contoso wants each participant to hear speech translated in real time, and wants live notes with action items captured during the meeting, using Microsoft-provided agents with no custom build. Which two agents should you enable? (Choose two.)
options: Facilitator
Interpreter
Researcher
Analyst
questions.explanation: Facilitator is the built-in meeting agent that keeps live notes and surfaces action items as the discussion happens, and Interpreter provides real-time speech translation in Teams meetings. Researcher performs multi-step research across work data and the web in Copilot Chat, and Analyst reasons over data and generates analysis; neither operates inside a live meeting.

questions.question: Before assigning any Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licenses, an admin wants to know how exposed the organization currently is to oversharing and identity hygiene gaps, so problems can be fixed ahead of rollout rather than discovered afterward. Which activity addresses this stage specifically?
options: Running a Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness assessment
Reviewing Microsoft 365 Copilot usage reports
Reviewing the Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard
Running DSPM for AI reports after the first month of usage
questions.explanation: A readiness assessment runs before rollout specifically to score factors like identity hygiene, device compliance, and oversharing risk so they can be addressed ahead of time. Usage reports and the Viva Insights Copilot Dashboard measure adoption after licenses are already assigned, and DSPM for AI reports on actual AI interactions, which requires usage to have already started.

questions.question: An organization wants to require a compliant device specifically before Microsoft 365 Copilot sign-in succeeds, while leaving its existing sign-in requirements for the rest of Microsoft 365 unchanged. How should this be configured?
options: Enabling security defaults, since it automatically applies stricter rules to Copilot only
A Conditional Access policy that targets the Enterprise Copilot Platform service principal as its own cloud app
A Purview DLP policy scoped specifically to Copilot interactions
The Allow web search in Copilot policy in Cloud Policy
questions.explanation: Because Microsoft 365 Copilot authenticates through the same Microsoft Entra sign-in as other Microsoft 365 apps, a Conditional Access policy can target its Enterprise Copilot Platform service principal (which may first need to be created so it appears in the app picker) as its own cloud app, layering a stricter device requirement onto Copilot sign-in without touching the rest of Microsoft 365. Security defaults apply one uncustomizable baseline to everything rather than singling out Copilot, a DLP policy governs content in responses rather than sign-in requirements, and the Allow web search in Copilot policy only controls whether Copilot searches the public web.

questions.question: Content a user writes into a Copilot Page is stored as a Loop file in the user's OneDrive and is within the scope of Purview eDiscovery.
questions.explanation: A Copilot Page is a durable Loop file stored in OneDrive (or SharePoint for shared contexts), so eDiscovery, retention, and audit cover it like other Microsoft 365 content. The misconception is that because a Page is not an email or a chat message, it falls outside compliance tooling.

questions.question: A Purview DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location prevents a Copilot Studio agent from using a Non-Business connector in the same action as a Business connector.
questions.explanation: Connector grouping and combination rules are enforced by Power Platform DLP policies, which govern what a Copilot Studio agent, flow, or app is allowed to call. Purview DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot governs sensitive content in Copilot interactions and has no concept of connector classification. The two 'DLP' features share a name but operate at different layers.

questions.question: Contoso licenses SharePoint Advanced Management and finds 40 overshared sites before its Copilot rollout. Which two actions rely on SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities? (Choose two.)
options: Run data access governance reports to find sites shared with 'Everyone except external users' and launch site access reviews
Apply restricted access control so only members of a Finance security group can access the Finance site
Enable Restricted SharePoint Search with an allowed list that leaves the 40 sites out of Copilot results
Create a DLP policy with the Microsoft 365 Copilot location to keep labeled content out of responses
questions.explanation: Data access governance reports and the site access reviews launched from them, together with restricted access control, are SharePoint Advanced Management features. Restricted SharePoint Search (being retired; successor: Restricted Content Discovery) is a tenant-level SharePoint setting that does not require the Advanced Management license, and a Copilot DLP policy is a Microsoft Purview capability; both help with a rollout but belong to different products.

questions.question: An employee is terminated and their Microsoft Entra account is immediately disabled. Minutes later, that employee's laptop — still holding a previously issued access token — attempts to open a SharePoint file. With Continuous Access Evaluation enabled, what happens?
options: Access is revoked almost immediately, since CAE evaluates the critical account-disabled event in near real time
Access continues working normally until the token's originally scheduled expiration time arrives
Access is revoked, but only once the next scheduled access review cycle happens to run
Access continues working until an admin separately issues a remote wipe of the laptop
questions.explanation: Continuous Access Evaluation re-evaluates a token near real time when a critical event like account disablement occurs, revoking access in roughly minutes rather than waiting out the token's full remaining lifetime. Without CAE, the token could otherwise keep working until it expires on its own schedule, and this has nothing to do with a periodic access review cycle or a separate remote wipe action.

questions.question: A document has been declared a regulatory record under Microsoft Purview Records Management. An admin later tries to remove its retention label to free up the document for editing. What happens?
options: The removal fails; neither the label nor the record's key properties can be changed before the retention period ends
The admin can remove the label right away, since admin accounts are exempt from records management locks
The label is removed, though the document's underlying content stays unchanged and still editable
The record is deleted automatically the instant anyone, including an admin, attempts to remove its label
questions.explanation: Declaring an item a regulatory record locks down both its label and key properties so that nobody, including an admin, can change or remove them until the retention period actually ends — a stronger guarantee than a standard retention label allows. Admin accounts are not exempt, no removal succeeds at all in this scenario, and no deletion is triggered by a blocked removal attempt.

questions.question: An Exact Data Match (EDM) sensitive information type flags any text that merely resembles a pattern, like digits shaped like a credit card number, regardless of whether that exact value is real.
questions.explanation: This describes a standard pattern-based sensitive information type, not EDM. An EDM sensitive information type instead checks content against an actual uploaded dataset of real values, catching only true matches and sharply reducing pattern-based false positives.

questions.question: Contoso publishes three retention labels in SharePoint: a standard label, a label that marks items as records, and a label that marks items as regulatory records. Which two statements about labeled documents are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: A regulatory record's label cannot be removed by anyone, including a Global Administrator, before the retention period ends
A document labeled as a record can be temporarily unlocked by an authorized user in SharePoint to edit its content
A document with the standard label cannot be deleted by any user, including its owner, until the retention period ends
A document labeled as a regulatory record can be unlocked for editing by an authorized user in the same way as a record
questions.explanation: Regulatory records are the most restrictive: the label cannot be removed or changed by anyone, and the content cannot be edited or unlocked. Records allow an authorized user to toggle the record lock in SharePoint to make edits, then re-lock the item. A standard retention label never blocks deletion; it preserves a copy in the Preservation Hold library instead, so the claim that a standard label blocks deletion describes record behavior, not standard-label behavior.

questions.question: An admin configures SSPR to require one authentication method to reset a password, and a user has registered two methods. The user then loses access to one of their two registered methods. What is the effect on their ability to reset their own password going forward?
options: They can still reset their password using their one remaining registered method, since only one method is required at reset time
They can no longer use self-service password reset at all until both original methods are restored
Their account is automatically disabled until a helpdesk agent manually re-registers both methods
SSPR requires exactly the same number of methods at reset as at registration, so losing one method blocks all self-service reset
questions.explanation: Registering more methods than a reset requires is deliberate — it gives a user more than one option to fall back on, so losing access to just one registered method still leaves them able to reset using the other. The reset step only requires the number of methods configured for reset (here one), not however many the user happened to register, and none of this disables the account automatically.

questions.question: An organization wants every self-service-created Microsoft 365 group to automatically carry a department-based prefix, and wants group names containing a list of specific blocked terms to be rejected outright at creation time. Which feature should be configured?
options: A Microsoft 365 Groups naming policy with a blocked words list
A Conditional Access policy scoped to the Groups creation experience
Entitlement management (access packages)
A Microsoft Entra dynamic group membership rule
questions.explanation: A groups naming policy enforces a required prefix or suffix convention and a separate blocked words list that rejects disallowed terms at creation time, matching both requirements directly. Conditional Access governs sign-in conditions rather than naming, entitlement management governs requesting access to existing resources rather than group creation naming, and a dynamic group rule only controls automatic membership, not naming conventions.

questions.question: Teams external access (federation) adds a user from another organization as a persistent member of a specific team, with ongoing access to that team's channels and files.
questions.explanation: That describes guest access, not external access. External access (federation) only lets users in separate tenants chat, call, and meet with each other without either becoming a member of the other tenant; persistent channel and file membership requires adding the user as an actual Entra B2B guest instead.

questions.question: Contoso's admin opens the Microsoft 365 admin center Home page shown, in Dashboard view. Leadership wants to know how many licensed users still have not installed the Microsoft 365 apps, and wants the admin to prompt them without visiting any device. Based on the Microsoft 365 apps card, which statement is accurate?
options: Three out of every four licensed users have not installed the apps, and the card offers an Email install link action to send them the install instructions
One out of every four licensed users has not installed the apps, and the card offers an Email install link action to send them the install instructions
Three out of every four licensed users have not installed the apps, and the toolbar action Add a user is the way to prompt them to install
One out of every four licensed users has not installed the apps, so no follow-up action is available from this page
questions.explanation: The card reads that 1 of 4 licensed users has installed the apps, so the remaining 3 of 4 (the Not Yet Installed share of the bar) have not. The same card carries Email install link, Install apps and Other install options buttons, so the admin can send installation instructions straight from the dashboard. Add a user in the toolbar creates new accounts and does nothing to prompt existing licensed users. Reading the figure the other way round (one in four not installed) inverts the card's 1-of-4 statement.
questions.whyTested: Admin center dashboard cards summarize state and expose the next action on the same card. This checks that you read the ratio correctly (installed versus not installed) and know the card's own actions rather than reaching for an unrelated toolbar command.

questions.question: An admin signs in to the Microsoft 365 admin center and sees the Home page shown, whose left navigation lists Home, Copilot, Users, Teams & groups, Marketplace, Billing and Setup. The admin needs the Settings menu to add a custom domain, but no Settings entry is visible. What should the admin select to reveal every menu available to them without changing how the navigation is configured?
options: Show all at the bottom of the left navigation
Customize navigation and save a new layout
Setup, to re-run the setup wizard
Copilot, to expand its submenu
